q.s: The Great Bath, a well-known structure of the Indus Valley Civilisation, was found at:
q.x: The Great Bath stood on the citadel mound of Mohenjodaro; Lothal is known for its dockyard.

q.s: The Great Bath of Mohenjodaro was made watertight with a layer of:
q.x: Burnt bricks set in gypsum mortar were sealed with a layer of bitumen to make the bath watertight.

q.s: Which of the following structures has NOT been clearly identified in Harappan cities?
q.x: No palaces or temples have been clearly found, unlike in Mesopotamia and Egypt, though granaries, drains and citadels are common.

q.s: The most common animal motif on Harappan seals is the:
q.x: The one-horned 'unicorn' is by far the commonest seal motif; the humped bull is rarer.

q.s: The tree most commonly depicted on Harappan seals is the:
q.x: The pipal leaf and tree appear most often on Harappan seals and pottery.

q.s: The 'Priest-King' statue from Mohenjodaro wears a shawl decorated with a:
q.x: The steatite Priest-King wears a shawl with a trefoil (three-lobed) design over the left shoulder.

q.s: The Hathigumpha inscription of Kharavela is found in the Udayagiri caves near:
q.x: The Hathigumpha ('elephant cave') inscription is in the Udayagiri hills near Bhubaneswar, Odisha.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Hathigumpha inscription is NOT correct?
o: It is written in the Kharosthi script.
It is an inscription of Kharavela.
It refers to the river Krishna as 'Kannabenna'.
It is found in the Udayagiri caves near Bhubaneswar.
q.x: The inscription is in Prakrit in the Brahmi script, not Kharosthi.

q.s: The Purusha Sukta, which describes the origin of the four varnas, is found in which Mandala of the Rigveda?
q.x: The Purusha Sukta is Rigveda X.90, a late addition in the 10th Mandala.

q.s: According to the Purusha Sukta, the Shudra was born from the Purusha's:
q.x: The Brahmana came from the mouth, the Rajanya from the arms, the Vaishya from the thighs and the Shudra from the feet.

q.s: In the Aitareya Brahmana, the term 'Ekarat' means:
q.x: Ekarat denotes the sole or paramount sovereign; Later Vedic kingship was becoming hereditary, not elective.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Later Vedic kingship is correct?
o: The king was chosen every year by the Sabha.
The term Ekarat meant a ruler elected by the Samiti.
The word 'rashtra' first appears in the family books of the Rigveda.
q.x: Kingship usually passed to the eldest son; Ekarat meant sole ruler, and 'rashtra' first appears in Later Vedic texts.

q.s: How many forms of marriage are listed by Manu and Kautilya?
q.x: Both list eight forms of marriage, of which the first four were approved.

q.s: In ancient Indian society, 'Anuloma' marriage was between:
o: A lower-varna man and a higher-varna woman
A higher-varna man and a lower-varna woman
q.x: Anuloma was the approved 'with the grain' union; the reverse (lower-varna man, higher-varna woman) was pratiloma.

q.s: The Vishishtadvaita school of Vedanta was propounded by:
q.x: Ramanuja taught Vishishtadvaita (qualified non-dualism); Madhva taught Dvaita.

q.s: Which of the following pairs of Vedanta school and teacher is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Dvaita was taught by Madhva; Nimbarka taught Dvaitadvaita.

q.s: Which dynasty was the last to extend royal support to Buddhism in Andhra?
q.x: The Vishnukundins (e.g. the Indrapalanagara vihara) were the last royal patrons of Buddhism in Andhra; the greatest patronage came under the Ikshvakus.

q.s: The Jain text Kalpasutra is ascribed to:
q.x: The Kalpasutra, containing the lives of the Tirthankaras, is attributed to Bhadrabahu.

q.s: Which of the following pairs of Jain work and author is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Kalyanakaraka, a medical work, was written by Ugradityacharya.

q.s: The 12th-century Virashaiva (Lingayat) movement, which weakened Jainism in Karnataka, was led by:
q.x: Basavanna led the Virashaiva movement in 12th-century Karnataka, dealing Jainism a serious blow.

q.s: Under the treaty with Seleucus Nicator, Chandragupta Maurya gave Seleucus:
q.x: Seleucus ceded Aria, Arachosia, Paropanisadai and Gedrosia and received 500 elephants.

q.s: Which of the following territories was NOT ceded by Seleucus Nicator to Chandragupta Maurya?
q.x: Seleucus ceded Aria, Arachosia, Paropanisadai and Gedrosia but retained Bactria.

q.s: Ashoka's coronation took place in about:
q.x: Ashoka acceded c. 273 BCE and was crowned about four years later, in 269 BCE; 261 BCE is the Kalinga war and 232 BCE his death.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Ashoka's accession is correct?
o: The Samantapasadika says he won Kalinga in Bindusara's time.
He was the son of Chandragupta Maurya.
The Mahavamsa says he killed 99 brothers in the succession struggle.
He was crowned in the same year as his accession.
q.x: The Mahavamsa speaks of 99 brothers killed; there was a gap of about four years between accession and coronation (269 BCE). He was Bindusara's son.

q.s: Ashoka's title 'Devanampiya' means:
q.x: Devanampiya means 'beloved of the gods'; Piyadasi means 'of pleasing looks'.

q.s: The name 'Ashoka' (as Buddhashakya Ashoka) occurs in which inscription?
q.x: The Maski minor rock edict (Raichur district) names the king as Ashoka; most edicts call him Devanampiya Piyadasi.

q.s: In Chola village administration, the term 'Kudavolai' referred to:
o: Selection by lot using palm-leaf ballots in a pot
q.x: Kudavolai was the pot-ticket lottery system used to choose committee members (variyapperumakkal).

q.s: Which of the following pairs relating to Chola village administration is NOT correctly matched?
o: Kudavolai — Selection by lot with palm-leaf tickets
q.x: The eri variyam was the tank committee.

q.s: In the Chola period, 'Brahmadeya' denoted:
q.x: Brahmadeya was tax-free land gifted to Brahmins; temple land was devadana and non-Brahmin peasant land vellanvagai.

q.s: Which of the following pairs of Chola land term and meaning is NOT correctly matched?
o: Brahmadeya — Rent-free land granted to Brahmins
Taniyur — Very large village administered as a separate unit
q.x: Vellanvagai was the land of non-Brahmin peasants.

q.s: Which general of Alauddin Khalji was killed during the first siege of Ranthambore?
q.x: Nusrat Khan was killed during the siege; Ranthambore fell in 1301.

q.s: Alauddin Khalji's policy towards the southern kingdoms was to:
o: Replace their kings with Khalji nobles
Collect wealth and tribute while leaving the kings on their thrones
Annex them and make them provinces
q.x: In the south Alauddin sought wealth and tribute; only the north was annexed.

q.s: Jalaluddin Khalji crowned himself in 1290 at:
q.x: Jalaluddin was crowned at Kilokhari in 1290 at about the age of 70.

q.s: Mongol converts settled near Delhi in the reign of Jalaluddin Khalji were called:
q.x: Mongols who embraced Islam and settled near Delhi were called 'New Mussalmans'.

q.s: The main source for Alauddin Khalji's market control measures is:
q.x: Barani gives the fullest account of the market regulations; Khusrau's Khazain-ul-Futuh describes the campaigns.

q.s: Alauddin Khalji's price controls were abolished by:
q.x: Qutbuddin Mubarak Shah (1316-20) abolished the price control and restored confiscated lands.

q.s: The 'Gaz-i-Sikandari', a yard for measuring land later used by Sher Shah and Akbar, was introduced by:
q.x: Sikandar Lodi introduced the Gaz-i-Sikandari; Akbar later introduced the Ilahi gaz.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Sikandar Lodi is correct?
o: He was the son of Ibrahim Lodi.
He had a Sanskrit work on medicine translated into Persian.
He had a Sanskrit work on astronomy translated into Persian.
q.x: Sikandar Lodi, son of Bahlol Lodi, had a medical work translated; the Ilahi gaz was Akbar's.

q.s: In his memoirs Babur described which ruler as the most powerful in India?
q.x: Babur praised the Vijayanagara ruler Krishnadevaraya as the most powerful ruler in India.

q.s: On his father's side Babur was descended from:
q.x: Babur descended from Timur on his father's side and from Chingiz Khan on his mother's side.

q.s: Akbar's Maktab Khana (House of Translation) was set up at:
q.x: The Maktab Khana was established at Fatehpur Sikri around 1574.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Akbar's court is NOT correct?
o: Sheikh Salim Chishti was the father of Abul Fazl and Faizi.
Birbal was killed in 1586 fighting the Yusufzai.
q.x: Abul Fazl and Faizi were sons of Sheikh Mubarak; Salim Chishti was the Sufi saint of Fatehpur Sikri.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Akbar's Din-i-Ilahi is correct?
o: It became the state religion of the Mughal Empire.
Akbar made it compulsory for all mansabdars.
It remained a small voluntary circle of followers.
It was promoted among the masses by Jahangir.
q.x: Din-i-Ilahi was never forced on anyone; it stayed a voluntary circle of about 18 members and never became a mass religion.

q.s: Who translated the Baburnama into Persian?
q.x: Abdur Rahim Khan-i-Khanan rendered the Turki Baburnama into Persian.

q.s: Which of the following Persian renderings is NOT correctly matched with its translator?
q.x: Lilavati was rendered into Persian by Faizi.

q.s: The Mughal emperor Shah Alam II was blinded in 1788 by:
q.x: Ghulam Qadir Rohilla blinded Shah Alam II in 1788; Najib-ud-Daula had died in 1770.

q.s: Shah Alam II returned to Delhi in 1771-72 under the protection of the:
q.x: Mahadji Scindia's Marathas escorted Shah Alam II back to Delhi in 1771-72.

q.s: In Mughal India, the head of a merchant community in a town was called the:
q.x: The Nagarseth headed the merchant community; Mahajans were moneylenders-cum-merchants.

q.s: Which of the following pairs of merchant group and role in Mughal India is NOT correctly matched?
o: Nagarseth — Head of a merchant community
Mahajans — Head of a merchant community
Seths and Bohras — Wholesale, long-distance trade
q.x: Mahajans were moneylenders-cum-merchants; the Nagarseth headed the community.

q.s: The musician Tansen was a disciple of:
q.x: Tansen learnt music under Swami Haridas of Vrindavan.

q.s: The tomb of Tansen is located at:
q.x: Tansen's tomb is at Gwalior; before joining Akbar he served Raja Ramchandra of Rewa.

q.s: Palkuriki Somanatha composed the Basava Puranam in which language?
q.x: Palkuriki Somanatha, the Virashaiva poet of Andhra, wrote the Basava Puranam in Telugu.

q.s: Which one of the following Bhakti saints is NOT correctly matched with his language?
q.x: Palkuriki Somanatha wrote in Telugu.

q.s: Shivaji's coronation in 1674 took place at:
q.x: Shivaji was crowned at Raigad in 1674 and took the title Chhatrapati.

q.s: Shivaji was crowned in 1674 by:
q.x: Gaga Bhatt of Banaras performed the coronation; Shivaji then started the Rajyabhisheka Shaka.

q.s: The charter of 1600 creating the English East India Company was granted by:
q.x: Queen Elizabeth I granted the charter on 31 December 1600 with a 15-year monopoly of eastern trade.

q.s: The first voyage of the English East India Company under James Lancaster (1601) set up a factory at:
q.x: Lancaster's voyage set up a factory at Bantam in Java; Surat came only in 1613.

q.s: Pondicherry, captured by the Dutch in 1693, was restored to the French by the Treaty of:
q.x: The Treaty of Ryswick (1697) restored Pondicherry to the French.

q.s: The former French settlement of Chandernagore joined India in 1950 through:
q.x: Chandernagore voted by plebiscite to join India in 1950.

q.s: The Inam Commission, which confiscated about 20,000 estates before the Revolt of 1857, was set up in which presidency?
q.x: The Inam Commission (1852) in Bombay confiscated about 20,000 estates; in Awadh taluqdars suffered under the Summary Settlement.

q.s: Which of the following statements about grievances before the Revolt of 1857 is correct?
o: The Inam Commission confiscated estates in Awadh.
Indian goods entered Britain duty-free while British goods were heavily taxed in India.
Peasants gained from low and flexible land revenue.
About 21,000 taluqdars of Awadh were dispossessed under the Summary Settlement.
q.x: Awadh taluqdars lost estates under the Summary Settlement; the Inam Commission was in Bombay, and British goods came duty-free while Indian goods were taxed.

q.s: Robert Clive captured Arcot in 1751 during the:
q.x: Clive seized Arcot in 1751 in the Second Carnatic War and held it for about 53 days against Raja Sahib.

q.s: Which Maratha chief fought on the English side during Clive's Carnatic campaign of 1751-52?
q.x: Morari Rao's Maratha troops helped the English during the Arcot campaign.

q.s: At the Battle of St. Thome (1746), the French under Captain Paradis defeated the army of the:
q.x: About 930 French troops routed some 10,000 men of Nawab Anwaruddin, who had sided with the English.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT among the powers defeated by the English at the Battle of Buxar (1764)?
q.x: At Buxar the English defeated Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-Daula and Shah Alam II together in open battle.

q.s: The first Dutch factory in Andhra was established at:
q.x: The Dutch set up their first Andhra factory at Machilipatnam (1605); Bhimunipatnam came later.

q.s: The first railway line in Andhra, opened in 1862, ran between:
q.x: The Puttur–Renigunta line, opened in 1862, was Andhra's first railway.

q.s: Life expectancy in India on the eve of independence was about:
q.x: Life expectancy was about 32 years and literacy under 16 per cent at independence.

q.s: Which of the following statements about India on the eve of independence is correct?
o: Agriculture contributed only about 30 per cent of GDP.
Per capita income was about Rs 20.
q.x: Literacy was under 16% and life expectancy about 32; per capita income was about Rs 265 and agriculture about half of GDP.

q.s: The cotton excise duty of 1894-96 in British India was levied on:
q.x: The excise was imposed on Indian mill cloth to offset the import duty on British goods, protecting Lancashire.

q.s: According to Paul Bairoch, India's share of world manufacturing output in 1750 was about:
q.x: Bairoch estimates it fell from about 24.5% in 1750 to under 2% in 1900.

q.s: Which famine in British India is known as the 'skull famine'?
q.x: The Doji Bara famine (1791-92) is called the skull famine because of the many unburied dead.

q.s: The Great Famine of 1876-78 in Madras, Mysore, Hyderabad and Bombay occurred during the viceroyalty of:
q.x: It occurred under Lytton, whose government was criticised for holding the Delhi Durbar of 1877 during the famine.

q.s: The journal 'Vivekavardhini' (1874) was started by:
q.x: Veeresalingam started Vivekavardhini in 1874 and Hasyasanjivani in 1876 to campaign for social reform.

q.s: Andhra Prakasika (1885), the first political weekly of Andhra, was started by:
q.x: A.P. Parthasarathy Naidu founded Andhra Prakasika in 1885.

q.s: The Lucknow Pact of 1916 between the Congress and the Muslim League was brokered mainly by:
q.x: Tilak and Jinnah were the chief architects of the Lucknow Pact.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Lucknow Pact (1916) is correct?
o: It accepted councils with nominated official majorities.
It rejected separate electorates for Muslims.
It merged the Congress and the Muslim League into one body.
It demanded that half the members of the executive councils be Indians.
q.x: The Pact was a joint reform scheme demanding elected majorities and half Indian executive councils; the Congress accepted separate electorates.

q.s: The first Justice Party ministry in Madras, formed in December 1920, was headed by:
q.x: Subbarayalu Reddiar headed the first ministry; the Raja of Panagal succeeded him as Premier in 1921. The Congress boycotted the 1920 elections.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Madras elections of 1920 is correct?
o: The first ministry was headed by the Raja of Panagal.
q.x: The Congress boycotted the first elections under the 1919 Act; the Justice Party formed the ministry under Subbarayalu Reddiar.

q.s: Krishna Patrika (1902) of Machilipatnam was founded by:
q.x: Konda Venkatappayya founded Krishna Patrika and was its first editor; Mutnuri Krishna Rao edited it later.

q.s: Nilagiri Patrika (1922), the first Telugu newspaper in Telangana, was published from:
q.x: Nilagiri Patrika was published from Nalgonda in 1922.

q.s: The Age of Consent Act, 1891 fixed the age of consent for girls at:
q.x: The Act made intercourse with a girl below 12 an offence, married or not.

q.s: Which of the following leaders opposed the Age of Consent Bill of 1891?
q.x: Tilak opposed it in Kesari as foreign interference in Hindu custom; the Moderates Ranade, Telang and Bhandarkar supported it.

q.s: The Poona Pact of 1932 was signed on behalf of the depressed classes by:
q.x: Ambedkar signed for the depressed classes and Madan Mohan Malaviya for the caste Hindus on 24 September 1932.

q.s: In September 1932 Gandhi undertook a fast unto death against the Communal Award while lodged in:
q.x: The 1932 fast was in Yerwada Jail, Poona; the Aga Khan Palace fast was in 1943.

q.s: The Hindu (Madras) was started in 1878 as a weekly by the:
q.x: A group of six young men of Triplicane, including G. Subramania Iyer, started it; it became a daily in 1889.

q.s: The English paper 'Crescent' (Madras, 1844) was founded by:
q.x: Gazula Lakshminarasu Chetty founded The Crescent in 1844 to voice Indian grievances.

q.s: P. Anandacharlu, the first Telugu President of the Indian National Congress, presided over which session?
q.x: Anandacharlu presided over the Nagpur session of 1891; he had attended the first session in 1885.

q.s: 'History of the Indian National Congress' was written by:
q.x: Bhogaraju Pattabhi Sitaramayya wrote the official History of the INC.

q.s: The 'safety-valve' theory of the origin of the INC was first mentioned in the biography of A.O. Hume written by:
q.x: Wedderburn's biography of Hume (1913) first mentioned it; Lajpat Rai used it in Young India (1916).

q.s: Which historian called the safety-valve theory a 'myth' and described Hume as a 'lightning conductor'?
q.x: Bipan Chandra rejected the theory; R.P. Dutt gave the Marxist conspiracy version.

q.s: The Bharat Mata Society was active in Punjab under the leadership of:
q.x: Ajit Singh, uncle of Bhagat Singh, led the Bharat Mata Society in Punjab.

q.s: The United Indian Patriotic Association (1888) of Sir Syed Ahmad Khan and Raja Shiv Prasad was formed to:
q.x: It was set up to counter the Congress and keep Muslims away from it.

q.s: Which of the following statements about M.A. Jinnah is correct?
o: He began his political career as an advocate of Hindu-Muslim unity.
He opposed the Lucknow Pact of 1916.
He championed the two-nation theory from the start of his career.
He founded the Muslim League in 1906.
q.x: Jinnah began as an 'ambassador of Hindu-Muslim unity' and helped make the Lucknow Pact; only after 1937 did he champion the two-nation theory.

q.s: The Chauri Chaura incident, after which Gandhi called off the Non-Cooperation Movement, took place in:
q.x: Chauri Chaura was in February 1922, after the Moplah uprising (August 1921) and the Prince of Wales boycott (November 1921).

q.s: The Moplah uprising of 1921 took place in:
q.x: The Moplah (Mappila) uprising broke out in Malabar in August 1921.

q.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: The Swaraj Party was formed on 1 January 1923 by C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru.

q.s: Gandhi's Salt March from Sabarmati to Dandi began on:
q.x: The march began on 12 March 1930; Gandhi broke the salt law at Dandi on 6 April. His letter to Irwin was dated 2 March.

q.s: On 31 January 1930 Gandhi placed before Lord Irwin a list of how many demands?
q.x: Gandhi's eleven demands included abolition of the salt tax and the salt monopoly.

q.s: Who described the Quit India Movement as a 'Spontaneous Revolution'?
q.x: F.G. Hutchins called it a 'Spontaneous Revolution' (1971).

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Quit India Movement is NOT correct?
o: No communal riots were recorded during it.
F.G. Hutchins called it a 'Spontaneous Revolution'.
The labour class stayed away from it altogether.
Textile workers of Ahmedabad went on strike for over three months.
q.x: Labour did join: strikes took place in Ahmedabad, Bombay, Jamshedpur, Ahmednagar and Poona.

q.s: The Cabinet Mission of 1946 was sent to India by British Prime Minister:
q.x: Attlee announced the mission on 19 February 1946; it reached Delhi on 24 March.

q.s: The Cabinet Mission Plan was announced on:
q.x: The plan was announced on 16 May 1946; 16 August was Direct Action Day and 3 June 1947 the Mountbatten Plan.

q.s: Who first put forward the demand for a Constituent Assembly for India in 1934?
q.x: M.N. Roy first raised the demand in 1934; the Congress adopted it officially in 1935.

q.s: The British government first accepted the demand for a Constituent Assembly in the:
q.x: The August Offer of 1940 first conceded the demand, before the Cripps Mission.

q.s: The Chirala-Perala movement against the municipal tax was led by:
q.x: Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya led it; it failed for lack of funds and leadership after his arrest following the Berhampur speech.

q.s: Who is known as 'Andhra Pitamaha'?
q.x: Madapati Hanumantha Rao is Andhra Pitamaha; Nyapathi Subba Rao is Andhra Bhishma.

q.s: Which of the following pairs of leader and title is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao was called Andhra Tilak.

q.s: The 1938 satyagraha against the ban on the Hyderabad State Congress was led by:
q.x: Swami Ramananda Tirtha led the State Congress satyagraha; Madapati Hanumantha Rao belongs to the Andhra Mahasabha.

q.s: Nagaland was granted statehood in:
q.x: Nagaland became the 16th state in 1963.

q.s: The Naga National Council (NNC) was led by:
q.x: A.Z. Phizo led the NNC; Laldenga led the Mizo National Front.

q.s: Total prohibition, introduced in Andhra Pradesh in 1995, was lifted in 1997 by Chief Minister:
q.x: NTR introduced total prohibition in 1995; Chandrababu Naidu lifted it in 1997.

q.s: The arrack ban of 1993 in Andhra Pradesh came under Chief Minister:
q.x: Following the anti-arrack movement, the 1993 arrack ban was imposed by Kotla Vijaya Bhaskara Reddy.

q.s: Andhra University was inaugurated in 1926 with its first headquarters at:
q.x: It began at Vijayawada in 1926 and moved to Waltair (Visakhapatnam), opening there in 1930.

q.s: Visakhapatnam was chosen in 1928 as the seat of Andhra University by the ministry of:
q.x: The Subbaroyan ministry chose Visakhapatnam over Vijayawada, Rajahmundry and Anantapur.

q.s: 'The Emergence of Andhra Pradesh' was written by:
q.x: K.V. Narayana Rao wrote The Emergence of Andhra Pradesh.

q.s: The Urdu newspaper 'Imroz', which opposed the Nizam's regime, was edited by:
q.x: Shoebullah Khan edited Imroz and was murdered in 1948; Mandumula Narsing Rao edited Rayyat.

q.s: The Srikrishna Committee on the Telangana issue, which offered six options, submitted its report on:
q.x: The report came on 30 December 2010; the Million March was in March 2011 and the CWC resolution in July 2013.

q.s: Which of the following events of the Telangana movement is NOT correctly matched with its year?
q.x: The Million March took place in March 2011.

q.s: The largest collection of anthropomorphic megaliths in Andhra is found in the region of:
q.x: Anthropomorphic megaliths are most numerous around Tirupati; menhirs cluster in Krishna district.

q.s: Which of the following statements about megalithic burials in Andhra is correct?
o: Megaliths are absent from Krishna district.
Anthropomorphic megaliths are found mainly in Srikakulam.
No dolmens are found in Chittoor.
Menhirs are concentrated in Krishna district.
q.x: Menhirs cluster in Krishna district, dolmens occur in Krishna and Chittoor, and anthropomorphic megaliths are most numerous around Tirupati.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the feudatories of the Satavahanas is correct?
o: The Mahabhojas were powerful local chiefs of the Konkan.
The Maharathis were found mainly in the eastern Deccan.
The Rajas could not issue coins.
The Mahabhojas ranked above the Rajas.
q.x: The Mahabhojas ruled in the Konkan; the Rajas, the highest feudatories, issued coins, and the Maharathis were mainly of the western Deccan.

q.s: Chamtisri, who rebuilt the Maha Chaitya at Nagarjunakonda and added ayaka pillars, belonged to which royal family?
q.x: Chamtisri was the sister of the Ikshvaku king Vasishthiputra Chamtamula; Ikshvaku women were great patrons of Buddhism.

q.s: The site of Nagarjunakonda was first excavated in 1927 by:
q.x: Longhurst excavated it first (1927-31); A. Ranganatha Saraswati discovered it in 1926 and R. Subrahmanyam dug there later.

q.s: Which of the following has NOT been found at Nagarjunakonda?
q.x: Nagarjunakonda has an amphitheatre, Santamula's Ashvamedha altar and viharas; the dockyard is at Lothal.

q.s: The Mogalrajapuram caves at Vijayawada were excavated under the:
q.x: The Mogalrajapuram caves are Vishnukundin excavations; the largest cave has a Nataraja figure.

q.s: At the Battle of Takkolam (949 CE), the Rashtrakuta king Krishna III defeated:
o: The Eastern Chalukya king Bhima I
q.x: Krishna III, helped by the Western Gangas and Vaidumbas, defeated Parantaka I; the Chola prince Rajaditya was killed.

q.s: The Eastern Chalukyas, who called themselves 'Haritiputras', worshipped which mother goddess?
q.x: The Eastern Chalukyas were Haritiputras and their mother goddess was Hariti; Kushmandini is a Jain yakshi.

q.s: The official language of the Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi was:
q.x: Sanskrit was their official language and most of their grants are in it, though Telugu literature rose under them.

q.s: Nannaya, who began the Telugu translation of the Mahabharata, was patronised by the Eastern Chalukya king:
q.x: Nannaya Bhattaraka was court poet of Rajaraja Narendra at Rajahmundry.

q.s: During the Pandavas' year in disguise (Ajnatavasa) in Virata's kingdom, Arjuna took the name:
q.x: Arjuna lived as Brihannala; Yudhishthira was Kanka and Bhima was Vallabha.

q.s: Which of the following pairs of Pandava and assumed name during the Ajnatavasa is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Yudhishthira lived as Kanka; Vallabha was Bhima's name.

q.s: 'Prataparudra Charitramu', a source for the late Kakatiya period, was written by:
q.x: Ekamranatha wrote Prataparudra Charitramu; Vidyanatha wrote Prataparudriyam.

q.s: Sakalya Malla was a court poet of:
q.x: Sakalya Malla adorned the court of Prataparudra II, the last Kakatiya king.

q.s: The first Vijayanagara ruler to attack Sri Lanka was:
q.x: Harihara II, the longest-reigning Sangama king, was the first to send an expedition to Sri Lanka.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Harihara II is correct?
o: He was the sole founder of the Vijayanagara empire.
He was killed at the battle of Talikota.
He was the longest-reigning king of the Sangama dynasty.
He belonged to the Saluva dynasty.
q.x: Harihara II was the longest-reigning Sangama king; his general Madhava took Goa.

q.s: Which Vijayanagara ruler took the title 'Vedamarga Pratishthapaka'?
q.x: Bukka I took this title; he also annexed Srisailam.

q.s: Saluva Mangu, the general of Bukka I who received the title 'Parapakshi Saluva', killed the Sultan of:
q.x: Saluva Mangu took part in Kumara Kampana's campaign that destroyed the Madurai Sultanate.

q.s: 'Parijatapaharanamu' was written by which of the Ashtadiggajas?
q.x: Nandi Timmana wrote Parijatapaharanamu; Peddana wrote Manucharitra.

q.s: Which of the following works is NOT correctly matched with its author?
q.x: Raghava Pandaviyamu, a dvyarthi kavya, was written by Pingali Surana.

q.s: In the Vijayanagara empire the marriage tax was first remitted by:
q.x: Saluva Narasimha was the first to remit the marriage tax.

q.s: In Vijayanagara times 'Meruka' was a tax on:
q.x: Meruka was levied on the sale and purchase of goods; market tax rights were auctioned to the Sunkandarlu.

q.s: Under the truce of 1364-65 with the Bahmanis, Kapaya Nayaka ceded:
q.x: Kapaya Nayaka ceded Golconda, paid 33 lakhs and presented the turquoise throne.

q.s: Kapaya Nayaka was killed in the battle of Bhimavaram by:
o: Anapota Nayaka of the Recherla family
q.x: Anapota Nayaka of the Recherla (Padmanayaka) family killed him at Bhimavaram.

q.s: Yanam, a former French enclave in Andhra, is today part of the Union Territory of:
o: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
q.x: Yanam joined India de facto in 1954 and de jure in 1962 and forms part of Puducherry.

q.s: The de jure transfer of Yanam to India took place in:
q.x: De facto transfer was in 1954; the treaty of cession took legal effect in 1962.

q.s: Kanneganti Hanumanthu, shot dead at Minchalapadu in February 1922, is associated with the:
q.x: Hanumanthu led the Palnadu forest satyagraha against the pullari and was shot during a cattle rescue.

q.s: The 'pullari', against which the Palnadu satyagraha was waged, was a tax on:
q.x: Pullari was the grazing fee of 12 annas a cow under the Forest Act of 1878.

q.s: The first woman President of the Indian National Congress was:
q.x: Annie Besant presided over the Calcutta session of 1917; Sarojini Naidu was the first Indian woman President (1925).

q.s: Annie Besant founded her Home Rule League in September 1916; Tilak's Home Rule League had been founded in:
q.x: Tilak started his League at Belgaum in April 1916, a few months before Besant's.

q.s: The title 'Granthalaya Pitamaha' was conferred on Ayyanki Venkata Ramanayya by the:
q.x: The Maharaja of Baroda honoured him; he led the library movement in Andhra.

q.s: Ayyanki Venkata Ramanayya edited the library journal:
q.x: He edited Grandhalaya Sarvasvam and was secretary of the Rama Mohana Library, Vijayawada.

q.s: The Rayalaseema Food and Dance Festival is held at:
q.x: It is held at Tirupati; Lepakshi Utsav also showcases Rayalaseema heritage.

q.s: Visakha Utsav is held on the Beach Road of Visakhapatnam by APTDC and:
q.x: The Visakhapatnam Metropolitan Region Development Authority co-organises the festival with APTDC.

q.s: The Girijan Cooperative Corporation (GCC) of Andhra was set up in:
q.x: The GCC was set up in 1956, before the Srikakulam tribal movement.

q.s: The Girijan Cooperative Corporation helped tribals mainly by:
o: Buying minor forest produce and supplying essentials
q.x: By buying minor forest produce and supplying essentials, the GCC freed tribals from moneylenders.

q.s: The Telugu film 'Sankarabharanam' was directed by:
q.x: K. Viswanath directed Sankarabharanam (1980); K.V. Reddy directed Pathala Bhairavi and B.N. Reddy Malliswari.

q.s: Which of the following pairs of Telugu film and director is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Pathala Bhairavi was directed by K.V. Reddy.

q.s: The Constitution of India came into force on:
q.x: It was adopted on 26 November 1949 (now Constitution Day) and came into force on 26 January 1950.

q.s: Constitution Day (Samvidhan Divas) is observed every year on:
q.x: 26 November, the day of adoption in 1949, was notified as Constitution Day in 2015.

q.s: Vande Mataram appeared in Bankim Chandra Chatterjee's novel Anandamath in:
q.x: It was composed in 1875 and published in Anandamath in 1882.

q.s: Vande Mataram was first sung at a session of the Indian National Congress in:
q.x: Rabindranath Tagore sang it at the Calcutta session of 1896.

q.s: Between Census 2001 and 2011, the share of nuclear households in urban India:
q.x: Urban nuclear households fell from 54.3% to 52.3%, while rural nuclear households rose from 50.7% to 52.1%.

q.s: Which sociologist identified 'companionate marriage' and 'serial monogamy' as contemporary trends in the Indian family?
q.x: Patricia Uberoi identified these trends in her work on family and marriage.

q.s: Under the Dr Ambedkar Scheme for Social Integration through Inter-Caste Marriages, a couple gets Rs 2.5 lakh when:
o: One of the spouses is a Dalit
The couple is below the poverty line
q.x: The incentive is given only when one spouse belongs to a Scheduled Caste.

q.s: Scheduled Tribes are defined in which Article of the Constitution?
q.x: Article 366(25) defines STs as communities deemed under Article 342; 366(24) defines SCs.

q.s: The first order specifying Scheduled Tribes under Article 342(1), the Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order, 1950, was issued by the:
q.x: The President notifies the first list; ST lists are State/UT-specific.

q.s: The term 'Scheduled Castes' was first used by the:
q.x: The Simon Commission first used the term; the first list followed in 1936.

q.s: The first list of Scheduled Castes was issued in 1936 under the:
q.x: The 1936 order was made under the Government of India Act, 1935.

q.s: Which Article of the Constitution fixes the time limit for the reservation of seats for SCs and STs in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies?
q.x: Article 334 sets the time limit (now up to 2030); Articles 330 and 332 provide the reservation itself.

q.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Article 342A — List of socially and educationally backward classes
q.x: Article 366(24) defines Scheduled Castes; 366(25) defines Scheduled Tribes.

q.s: In which case did the Supreme Court, dealing with child labour in Sivakasi, order a Child Labour Rehabilitation-cum-Welfare Fund?
o: Independent Thought v. Union of India (2017)
Bachpan Bachao Andolan v. Union of India (2011)
M.C. Mehta v. State of Tamil Nadu (1996)
q.x: M.C. Mehta (1996) banned child labour in hazardous industries and directed Rs 20,000 per child into the fund.

q.s: Which of the following pairs of case and ruling is NOT correctly matched?
o: Bachpan Bachao Andolan (2011) — Child labour in construction violates Fundamental Rights
PUDR v. Union of India (1982) — Child labour in construction violates Fundamental Rights
Independent Thought (2017) — Marital-rape exception for wives below 18
M.C. Mehta v. State of Tamil Nadu (1996) — Child labour in Sivakasi
q.x: Bachpan Bachao Andolan dealt with trafficking, child begging and circus children.

q.s: The CBSE 'Udaan' scheme aims to increase the enrolment of girls in:
q.x: Udaan supports girl students preparing for premier engineering institutions.

q.s: 1990 was observed as the Year of the Girl Child by:
q.x: SAARC observed 1990 as the Year of the Girl Child (and 1991-2000 as the Decade of the Girl Child).

q.s: K. Prithika Yashini is known as India's first transgender:
q.x: Prithika Yashini became a sub-inspector in Tamil Nadu; Manabi Bandyopadhyay was the first transgender college principal.

q.s: Which of the following pairs of person and 'first' is NOT correctly matched?
o: K. Prithika Yashini — First transgender police sub-inspector
Madhu Bai Kinnar — First openly transgender mayor
q.x: Manabi Bandyopadhyay was the first transgender college principal.

q.s: Under MGNREGA, what minimum share of the beneficiaries was to be women?
q.x: At least one-third of workers were to be women everywhere, not only in Scheduled Areas.

q.s: Which of the following statements about MGNREGA is NOT correct?
o: Social audits were conducted by the Gram Sabha.
The one-third share for women applied only in Scheduled Areas.
Works were planned and carried out by the Gram Panchayat.
It has been repealed by the VB-G RAM G Act.
q.x: The one-third share for women applied everywhere.

q.s: 'Talliki Vandanam', one of the Super Six guarantees of Andhra Pradesh, replaced:
q.x: Talliki Vandanam replaced Amma Vodi and covers children in government and private schools.

q.s: Under Talliki Vandanam, the annual assistance given is:
o: ₹15,000 per mother, whatever the number of children
q.x: The scheme gives ₹15,000 for every school-going child, aiming to raise the Gross Enrolment Ratio.

q.s: Which Supreme Court judgment of March 2018 required a preliminary enquiry before registering an FIR under the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act?
q.x: Mahajan required a preliminary enquiry by a DSP; it was recalled on review in October 2019.

q.s: To undo the Mahajan directions, the SC/ST (PoA) Amendment Act, 2018 inserted Section:
q.x: Section 18A removed the need for a preliminary enquiry or prior approval for arrest.

q.s: 'Operation Meghdoot' (April 1984) of the Indian Army related to:
q.x: Meghdoot secured the Siachen Glacier; Operation Vijay was the Kargil conflict of 1999.

q.s: Which of the following pairs of operation and conflict is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Operation Vijay was the Kargil conflict of 1999; Trident was the 1971 naval attack on Karachi.

q.s: India's Kirthai-II and Sawalkote hydroelectric projects are on the river:
q.x: Both projects are on the Chenab, a western river under the Indus Waters Treaty.

q.s: The McMahon Line, the eastern boundary claimed by India with China, was drawn at the:
q.x: The McMahon Line was drawn at the Simla Convention, 1914; China rejects it.

q.s: According to the Johnson Line of 1865, which represents India's claim, Aksai Chin lies in:
q.x: The Johnson Line places Aksai Chin in Ladakh; China occupies about 38,000 sq km there.

q.s: 'Shaheen' is a joint exercise between China and Pakistan involving their:
q.x: Shaheen is the air force exercise; Warrior is the army and Sea Guardian the navy exercise.

q.s: The Yarlung Tsangpo, on which China is building a mega dam, enters India in Arunachal Pradesh as the:
q.x: The Yarlung Tsangpo becomes the Siang and then the Brahmaputra, so India is concerned about downstream flows.

q.s: Which Article of the UN Charter deals with voting in the Security Council, including the veto of the permanent members?
q.x: Article 27 requires the 'concurring votes of the permanent members'; Article 2 lays down sovereign equality.

q.s: Which of the following Articles of the UN Charter is NOT correctly matched?
o: Article 23 — Veto of the permanent members
Article 27 — Voting in the Security Council
Article 18 — Two-thirds majority for important questions in the UNGA
q.x: Article 23 bars immediate re-election of retiring non-permanent members; the veto is in Article 27.

q.s: The World Trade Organization came into existence on 1 January 1995 under the:
q.x: The Marrakesh Agreement (1994) concluded the Uruguay Round and created the WTO.

q.s: The Dunkel Draft (1991) was part of which round of GATT negotiations?
q.x: The Uruguay Round, the eighth GATT round, produced the Dunkel Draft.

q.s: The Regulating Act, the first step by the British Parliament to control the East India Company, was passed in:
q.x: Regulating Act 1773, Pitt's India Act 1784, Charter Acts 1793 and 1813.

q.s: Which of the following Acts was NOT passed in the 18th century?
q.x: The Regulating Act (1773), Pitt's India Act (1784) and the Charter Act of 1793 were 18th-century Acts.

q.s: Who was the temporary President of the Constituent Assembly of India?
q.x: As the eldest member, Sachchidananda Sinha was temporary President, following French practice.

q.s: The first draft of the Constitution (October 1947), with 243 Articles and 13 Schedules, was prepared by:
q.x: B.N. Rau, the Constitutional Adviser, prepared it; he later became a judge of the International Court of Justice.

q.s: In which case did the Supreme Court hold that a society running a Regional Engineering College is 'State', the test being creation and control rather than legal form?
o: R.D. Shetty v. International Airport Authority
q.x: Ajay Hasia (1981) applied the R.D. Shetty tests to hold the REC society to be State under Article 12.

q.s: Article 12 of the Indian Constitution defines:
q.x: Article 12 defines 'the State' for Part III; Article 13 deals with 'law'.

q.s: The right to travel abroad was held to be part of personal liberty under Article 21 in:
q.x: Satwant Singh Sawhney linked the right to go abroad with personal liberty.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Article 21 is correct?
o: The Supreme Court held in 2023 that there is an unqualified fundamental right to marry.
Its protection is available to citizens and non-citizens alike.
It can be suspended during a National Emergency.
Its protection is available only to citizens.
q.x: Article 21 covers every person; after the 44th Amendment Articles 20 and 21 cannot be suspended, and Supriyo Chakraborty found no unqualified right to marry.

q.s: Preventive detention means:
o: Detention of illegal foreign nationals only
Detention without trial on suspicion of future harmful acts
Detention after conviction by a court
q.x: Preventive detention is meant for public order, not routine law and order.

q.s: At present, a person under preventive detention may be held without the report of an Advisory Board for up to:
q.x: The 44th Amendment's cut to two months was never brought into force, so Article 22(4)'s three-month limit applies.

q.s: In which case did an 11-judge Bench of the Supreme Court hold that minority status is to be determined State-wise?
q.x: T.M.A. Pai held that linguistic and religious minorities are to be identified State-wise.

q.s: Which of the following pairs of case and holding is NOT correctly matched?
o: P.A. Inamdar (2005) — RTE 25% quota not for minority schools
T.M.A. Pai Foundation (2002) — Minority status decided State-wise
In re Kerala Education Bill (1958) — Presidential reference
Pramati Educational Trust (2014) — RTE 25% quota not for minority schools
q.x: P.A. Inamdar held there could be no State reservation in unaided private colleges, leading to the 93rd Amendment.

q.s: The Mandal Commission recommendations were implemented in 1990 by the government of:
q.x: The V.P. Singh (National Front) government implemented them in August 1990.

q.s: The Second Backward Classes Commission (Mandal Commission) was set up by the government of:
q.x: The Janata government of Morarji Desai set it up (decided 1978, constituted 1979).

q.s: The first Chairperson of the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights was:
q.x: Shantha Sinha was the first Chairperson of the NCPCR (2007).

q.s: The NCPCR was set up in 2007 under the:
o: Commissions for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005
q.x: It was constituted in 2007 under the CPCR Act, 2005; it has the powers of a civil court.

q.s: Article 15(4) was inserted by the First Amendment (1951) in response to which judgment?
o: Romesh Thappar v. State of Madras
Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala
State of Madras v. Champakam Dorairajan
A.K. Gopalan v. State of Madras
q.x: Champakam Dorairajan struck down communal reservation; Article 15(4) enabled special provisions for backward classes, SCs and STs.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Article 15(4) is correct?
o: It was inserted in response to Romesh Thappar.
It applies only to Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
It overcame the bar of Article 30(2).
It covers socially and educationally backward classes besides SCs and STs.
q.x: Article 15(4) responded to Champakam Dorairajan and overcame Article 29(2).

q.s: Fundamental Duties of citizens are listed in which Article of the Constitution?
q.x: Article 51A lists the Fundamental Duties; Article 51 is a Directive Principle on international peace.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Fundamental Duties is correct?
o: They are enforceable in courts like Fundamental Rights.
They were part of the original Constitution of 1950.
Article 51A(e) refers to the spirit of common brotherhood.
q.x: Article 51A(e) speaks of common brotherhood; the duties were added by the 42nd Amendment, 1976.

q.s: A Bill to change the name of a State, such as the Kerala (Alteration of Name) Bill, is brought under:
q.x: Changes of name and boundaries of States are made by ordinary law under Article 3, not as constitutional amendments.

q.s: The Andhra State Bill, introduced on 10 August 1953, received the President's assent on:
q.x: Assent came on 14 September 1953; Andhra State was formed on 1 October 1953.

q.s: Nominated members of the Rajya Sabha can vote in the election of the:
o: Both the President and the Vice-President
Neither the President nor the Vice-President
q.x: Nominated members form part of the Vice-President's electoral college but not the President's.

q.s: A nominated member of the Rajya Sabha may join a political party within how many months of taking his seat without disqualification?
q.x: Under the Tenth Schedule a nominated member may join a party within six months.

q.s: Which of the following statements about prorogation of the Houses of Parliament is correct?
o: The Speaker prorogues the House under Article 85.
All pending Bills lapse on prorogation.
After prorogation the Speaker can summon the House.
Pending Bills do not lapse on prorogation.
q.x: The President prorogues under Article 85(2)(a) on ministerial advice; pending Bills survive prorogation and only the President can summon the House again.

q.s: The first no-confidence motion in the Lok Sabha was moved in 1963 against the Nehru government by:
q.x: Acharya J.B. Kripalani moved the first no-confidence motion in August 1963; notice is given in writing to the Secretary-General.

q.s: The no-confidence motion of November 1954 in the Andhra State Assembly brought down the ministry of:
q.x: The Prakasam ministry fell 69–68 and President's Rule followed; Bezawada Gopala Reddy became Chief Minister in 1955.

q.s: The Contingency Fund of India is held on behalf of the President by the Finance Secretary of the:
q.x: The fund is held by the Secretary, Department of Economic Affairs; its corpus is Rs 30,000 crore from 2021-22.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Contingency Fund of India is correct?
o: It was created by an Act of Parliament in 1950.
It is placed at the disposal of the Prime Minister.
It forms part of the Consolidated Fund of India.
It is not audited by the CAG.
q.x: It was created by the Contingency Fund of India Act, 1950, is at the disposal of the President, and is audited by the CAG.

q.s: A cut motion that seeks to reduce a demand for grant to Re 1, expressing disapproval of the policy behind it, is called a:
q.x: A policy cut reduces the demand to Re 1; a token cut reduces it by Rs 100 to air a specific grievance.

q.s: 'Guillotine' in the budget procedure of Parliament means:
o: Putting all remaining demands to vote without discussion on the last allotted day
Referring the demands to a Standing Committee
Reducing a demand by Rs 100 to air a grievance
q.x: On the last allotted day the Speaker puts all undiscussed demands to vote together.

q.s: Under the Provisional Collection of Taxes Act, 1931, the Finance Bill must be enacted within:
q.x: The Finance Bill must be passed and assented to within 75 days of its introduction.

q.s: Which of the following statements about amendments to the Finance Bill is correct?
o: They can be moved only in the Rajya Sabha.
They may increase an existing tax.
They may reduce or abolish a tax but cannot increase it.
They are not allowed at all.
q.x: Amendments to the Finance Bill can only reduce or abolish a tax, not raise it.

q.s: The Andhra Pradesh Official Language Act, which made Telugu the official language of the State, was passed in:
q.x: The AP Official Language Act, 1966 made Telugu the official language.

q.s: Under Article 174(1), a session of the State Legislature is summoned by the:
q.x: The Governor summons the House under Article 174(1); the Speaker cannot.

q.s: The Chairman and members of a State Public Service Commission are appointed by the Governor but can be removed only by the:
o: Chief Justice of the High Court
q.x: SPSC members are appointed by the Governor but removable only by the President.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT appointed by the Governor of a State?
o: Chairman of the State Public Service Commission
q.x: High Court judges are appointed by the President; the Governor appoints District Judges in consultation with the High Court.

q.s: Which commission on Centre-State relations recommended that Article 356 be used only as a last resort?
q.x: The Sarkaria Commission (1983-88) said Article 356 should be used sparingly, as a last resort.

q.s: Which body recommended a 'localised emergency' in a district for up to three months?
q.x: The Punchhi Commission (2007-10) proposed localised emergencies and fixed tenure for Governors.

q.s: A Rajya Sabha resolution under Article 249, enabling Parliament to legislate on a State List subject, must be passed by:
o: Two-thirds of the members present and voting
An absolute majority of the total membership
Three-fourths of the members present and voting
q.x: Article 249 needs a two-thirds majority of members present and voting.

q.s: A resolution passed by the Rajya Sabha under Article 249 remains in force for:
q.x: The resolution lasts one year at a time and can be renewed; the law lapses six months after it ends.

q.s: Parliament can make laws on any subject, including State subjects, to implement international treaties and agreements under:
q.x: Article 253 covers implementing international agreements; Article 250 applies during a National Emergency.

q.s: Under Article 252, Parliament may legislate on a State subject when:
o: President's Rule is in force in a State
Two or more States request it by resolution
A National Emergency is in operation
The Rajya Sabha passes a resolution in the national interest
q.x: Article 252 applies when two or more State Legislatures pass resolutions requesting Parliament to legislate.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a 'coming-together' federation?
q.x: India, like Spain and Belgium, is a holding-together federation where a large country divides power with a strong Centre.

q.s: A loose league of sovereign States that keep the right to secede is called a:
q.x: In a confederation member States retain sovereignty and the right to secede.

q.s: Which of the following Acts was enacted by Parliament under Article 252?
q.x: The Wild Life (Protection) Act was made on the request of States under Article 252; the Environment Protection Act was made under Article 253.

q.s: A law made by Parliament under Article 252 can be amended or repealed by:
o: The State Legislatures that requested it
Either Parliament or the State Legislatures
q.x: Only Parliament can amend or repeal an Article 252 law, even for the requesting States.

q.s: Which Article of the Constitution gives Parliament the exclusive power to make GST laws on inter-State supply of goods and services?
q.x: Article 246A(2) gives Parliament exclusive power over inter-State GST; Article 279A creates the GST Council.

q.s: The Union List of the Seventh Schedule, which originally had 97 subjects, now has:
q.x: The Union List now has 98 entries and the Concurrent List 52.

q.s: The award period of the Sixteenth Finance Commission is:
q.x: The 16th FC covers 2026-31; the 15th covered 2020-21 and 2021-26, and the 14th 2015-20.

q.s: Which of the following pairs of Finance Commission and award period is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: The 14th FC covered 2015-20.

q.s: Max Weber's ideal-type bureaucracy rests on which type of authority?
q.x: Weber's bureaucracy is impersonal and merit-based, resting on legal-rational authority.

q.s: Who classified bureaucracy into guardian, caste, patronage and merit types?
q.x: Fritz Morstein Marx gave this four-fold classification.

q.s: The three-stage Civil Services Examination (from 1979) was introduced on the recommendation of the:
q.x: The Kothari Committee (1976) recommended the preliminary, main and interview stages.

q.s: Which of the following pairs of committee and focus is NOT correctly matched?
o: D.S. Kothari Committee — Three-stage Civil Services Examination
B.S. Baswan Committee — Age limit, attempts and pattern
q.x: The Hota Committee (2004) dealt with domain expertise, lateral entry and appraisal.

q.s: The Chairperson of a State Human Rights Commission can be removed by the:
q.x: Though appointed by the Governor, SHRC Chairpersons and members are removed only by the President.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Human Rights Commissions is NOT correct?
o: The SHRC Chairperson submits his resignation to the President.
The SHRC Chairperson is appointed by the Governor.
The NHRC Chairperson submits his resignation to the President.
The NHRC Chairperson is appointed by the President.
q.x: The SHRC Chairperson resigns to the Governor, though only the President can remove him.

q.s: Since the 2019 amendment, the NHRC consists of a Chairperson and how many full-time members?
q.x: There are five full-time members, including a Supreme Court Judge, a High Court Chief Justice and three human rights experts (at least one woman).

q.s: Which of the following statements about the NHRC is correct?
o: It has no requirement of a woman member.
Its Secretary-General exercises administrative and financial powers.
Its members include the serving Chief Justice of India.
q.x: The Secretary-General has administrative and financial, not judicial, powers; at least one human-rights member must be a woman.

q.s: A judicial inquiry into a custodial death, mandatory under Section 176(1A) of the old CrPC, is now provided under BNSS Section:
q.x: BNSS s.196 carries over the mandatory judicial inquiry; s.218 deals with sanction for prosecuting public servants.

q.s: The first Lokpal of India, appointed in March 2019, was:
q.x: Justice P.C. Ghose was appointed on 19 March 2019.

q.s: Which of the following pairs relating to the Lokpal is NOT correctly matched?
o: Justice A.M. Khanwilkar — Chairperson since March 2024
Prashant Mishra — Designer of the Lokpal logo
q.x: Sushil Chandra, former CEC, is a non-judicial member.

q.s: The first Lokpal Bill was introduced in the Lok Sabha in:
q.x: It was introduced in the Fourth Lok Sabha in 1968, passed in 1969, and lapsed on the dissolution of the House.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the first Lokpal Bill is correct?
o: It was rejected by the Rajya Sabha.
It lapsed on the dissolution of the Lok Sabha.
It was introduced in the Rajya Sabha.
q.x: It passed the Lok Sabha in 1969 and lapsed when the House was dissolved before the Rajya Sabha passed it.

q.s: Under the Prevention of Corruption (Amendment) Act, 2018, a public servant convicted of taking a bribe faces imprisonment of:
q.x: The 2018 Act prescribes 3 to 7 years and a fine, and makes commercial organisations liable for bribes.

q.s: Under the 2018 amendment, trial of a corruption case must be completed within 2 years, extendable up to a maximum of:
q.x: The 2-year limit can be extended, but the total cannot exceed 4 years.

q.s: Each Zonal Council is chaired by the:
o: Chief Minister of the host State
q.x: The Union Home Minister chairs every Zonal Council; Chief Ministers act as vice-chairmen by rotation.

q.s: The Zonal Councils were set up under the:
q.x: They are statutory, advisory bodies created by the States Reorganisation Act, 1956, on Nehru's suggestion.

q.s: The Business Reform Action Plan (BRAP) ranking of States is released by:
q.x: BRAP rankings are released by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade.

q.s: In BRAP 2019 (released in September 2020), which State was ranked first?
q.x: Andhra Pradesh topped, followed by Uttar Pradesh and Telangana.

q.s: According to the Sarkaria Commission, a doubt about a Ministry's majority should be settled by:
o: A floor test in the House
q.x: Sarkaria held that a doubtful majority must be tested on the floor of the House.

q.s: In which case did the Supreme Court rely on the Sarkaria report to limit the use of Article 356?
o: S.R. Bommai v. Union of India (1994)
q.x: S.R. Bommai (and later Rameshwar Prasad, 2006) drew on the Sarkaria recommendations.

q.s: The Ashok Mehta Committee (1977-78) recommended a:
o: Three-tier system with the block as the key unit
Single-tier system at the village level
q.x: Ashok Mehta proposed a two-tier system with the district as the key unit.

q.s: Which of the following was a recommendation of the Ashok Mehta Committee?
o: Official participation of political parties in panchayat elections
Keeping political parties out of panchayat elections
Social audit of panchayats by the CAG
q.x: It favoured official party participation, elections within six months of supersession, and a Minister for Panchayati Raj.

q.s: The grants recommended by the Sixteenth Finance Commission (2026-31) are only for:
q.x: The 16th FC dropped revenue-deficit, sector-specific and State-specific grants.

q.s: The State Finance Commission is constituted every five years by the:
q.x: Under Articles 243I and 243Y the Governor constitutes the State Finance Commission.

q.s: Which Article extends the State Finance Commission's review to the finances of Municipalities?
q.x: Article 243I covers Panchayats and 243Y Municipalities; 243K and 243ZA deal with State Election Commissions.

q.s: The term 'Washington Consensus' (1989) was coined by:
q.x: John Williamson coined it for a package of reforms including financial liberalisation and a competitive exchange rate.

q.s: The Washington Consensus was associated with the IMF, the World Bank and the:
q.x: The three Washington-based institutions were the IMF, the World Bank and the US Treasury.

q.s: Inter-State electricity tariffs in India are fixed by the:
q.x: CERC handles inter-State matters; SERCs handle intra-State ones. CERC also regulates carbon trading.

q.s: The Andhra Pradesh Electricity Regulatory Commission was constituted in 1999 under the:
q.x: APERC was set up in 1999 under the State's Electricity Reform Act of 1998.

q.s: The Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) is an example of a:
q.x: CII is a business pressure group; the Bharatiya Kisan Union is agrarian.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a trade union?
q.x: The Indian Medical Association is a professional group; the others are trade unions.

q.s: India's first National Water Policy was adopted in:
q.x: The first NWP came in 1987, followed by policies in 2002 and 2012.

q.s: The Jal Shakti Abhiyan, focusing on 256 water-stressed districts, was launched in:
q.x: Jal Shakti Abhiyan began in 2019.

q.s: Under the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014, the Polavaram irrigation project was declared a national project by Section:
q.x: Section 90 makes Polavaram a national project; Section 89 extends the KWDT term and Section 91 concerns the Tungabhadra Board.

q.s: Which of the following sections of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 is NOT correctly matched with its subject?
o: Section 89 — Extension of the KWDT's term
q.x: Section 91 concerns the Tungabhadra Board; Polavaram is under Section 90.

q.s: The Infrastructure PPP Adjudication Tribunal was proposed by the committee headed by:
q.x: The Kelkar Committee (2015) on revitalising PPPs proposed it.

q.s: The Deepak Parekh Committee (2007) dealt with:
q.x: The Parekh Committee examined infrastructure financing.

q.s: Which sector has the largest share in the National Infrastructure Pipeline (NIP)?
q.x: Energy has the largest share of the NIP's about ₹111 lakh crore investment over FY2020-25.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the National Infrastructure Pipeline is correct?
o: The Centre was to fund about 21% of it.
The private sector was to fund about 39% of it.
It covers both economic and social infrastructure.
q.x: The NIP covers economic and social infrastructure; the Centre was to fund about 39%, the States 40% and the private sector 21%.

q.s: The headquarters of the South Coast Railway zone is at:
q.x: SCoR, created after the AP Reorganisation Act, is headquartered at Visakhapatnam.

q.s: Before the South Coast Railway, India's 17th railway zone was:
q.x: Metro Railway, Kolkata became the 17th zone; SCoR was the 18th.

q.s: India launched its National Family Planning Programme in:
q.x: India was the first country to launch a national family planning programme, in 1952; it was renamed Family Welfare in 1977.

q.s: The target-free approach in India's family planning programme was adopted in:
q.x: The target-free approach came in 1996, followed by the RCH approach in 1997.

q.s: The idea of the 'Right to the City' is associated with:
q.x: Henri Lefebvre put forward the idea in 1968.

q.s: UN-Habitat, which publishes the World Cities Report, is most directly linked to which Sustainable Development Goal?
q.x: SDG 11 is on sustainable cities and communities; SDG 13 is climate action.

q.s: Under MGNREGA, if work is not given within 15 days of application, the unemployment allowance for the first 30 days is:
q.x: It is one-fourth of the wage for the first 30 days and one-half thereafter.

q.s: Under Section 17 of MGNREGA, regular social audits of works are conducted by the:
q.x: Section 17 makes the Gram Sabha responsible for social audits.

q.s: Under GeoMGNREGA, assets created under the scheme are geo-tagged using ISRO's platform:
q.x: GeoMGNREGA uses the Bhuvan platform; Andhra Pradesh tracked fund flow on RAGA soft.

q.s: Which of the following pairs relating to MGNREGA is NOT correctly matched?
o: Section 21 — Social audit by the Gram Sabha
RAGA soft — Fund-flow monitoring in Andhra Pradesh
Section 17 — Social audit by the Gram Sabha
q.x: Section 21 deals with the State Employment Guarantee Fund.

q.s: Which of the following programmes was NOT merged into the Swarnjayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (1999)?
q.x: SGSY merged IRDP, TRYSEM, DWCRA, SITRA, GKY and the Million Wells Scheme; RLEGP had earlier merged into the Jawahar Rozgar Yojana.

q.s: In 2011 the SGSY was restructured as the:
q.x: SGSY, a Ministry of Rural Development scheme, became NRLM (Aajeevika) in 2011.

q.s: The National Social Assistance Programme (1995) gives effect to the Directive Principle in:
q.x: Article 41 asks the State to provide public assistance in old age, sickness and disablement; NSAP is a 'Core of the Core' scheme.

q.s: The National Social Assistance Programme is implemented by the Ministry of:
q.x: NSAP is run by the Ministry of Rural Development.

q.s: Under the Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana, the annual premium for a life cover of ₹2 lakh is:
q.x: PMJJBY (age 18-50) costs ₹436 a year; PMSBY's premium was raised from ₹12 to ₹20.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana is correct?
o: It covers only accidental death or disability.
It has fewer enrolments than PMJJBY.
q.x: PMSBY pays ₹2 lakh for accidental death or total disability only; natural death is covered by PMJJBY. PMSBY has more enrolments.

q.s: AMRUT 2.0 aims at universal water supply in:
q.x: AMRUT 2.0 extends universal water supply to all statutory towns.

q.s: The original AMRUT mission was launched in:
q.x: AMRUT ran from 2015-16 to 2019-20 with an outlay of Rs 1 lakh crore; JNNURM was launched in 2005.

q.s: The theme of the Economic Survey 2025-26 is:
q.x: ES 2025-26 is themed 'Building Strategic Indispensability'; 'Saving Lives and Livelihoods' was the 2020-21 theme.

q.s: Under Section 93 of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014, the Centre must take the measures in the Thirteenth Schedule within:
q.x: Section 93 gives ten years from the appointed day for the Thirteenth Schedule measures.

q.s: At Independence, agriculture contributed about what share of India's GDP?
q.x: Agriculture gave about half of GDP in 1947; by 2017-18 it was about 17% against services' 54%.

q.s: Which of the following statements about agriculture's share in India's GDP is correct?
o: In 2017-18 agriculture contributed about 17 per cent.
In 1991 agriculture contributed more than services.
Agriculture now contributes more GVA than services.
At Independence agriculture contributed about one-tenth.
q.x: Agriculture was about half at Independence, about 29% in 1991 (below services) and about 17% in 2017-18.

q.s: The 'usual status (ps+ss)' measure of employment uses a reference period of:
q.x: Usual status uses 365 days; current weekly status uses 7 days.

q.s: The percentage of the population that is employed is called the:
q.x: WPR is the share of population employed; LFPR includes those seeking or available for work.

q.s: The calorie norm of 2,400 kcal for rural and 2,100 kcal for urban areas was used by the:
q.x: The Alagh norm is 2,400/2,100 kcal; Dandekar-Rath used 2,250 kcal for both.

q.s: In India, the poverty line is based on consumption expenditure rather than income mainly because:
o: Income data are collected only in the Census
Incomes of the self-employed and daily-wage workers are hard to measure and vary with seasons
Consumption is always higher than income
q.x: Consumption is used because incomes of the self-employed and casual workers are hard to judge and seasonal.

q.s: The Mahalanobis model gave top priority to:
q.x: It stressed basic and heavy industries and left consumer goods to small and cottage industry.

q.s: Which Five-Year Plan was based on the Mahalanobis model?
q.x: The Second Plan (1956-61) followed the Mahalanobis model; the First was based on the Harrod-Domar model.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a feature of the Mahalanobis model?
o: An open economy relying on export promotion
A four-sector division of the economy
Consumer goods left largely to household industry
q.x: The Mahalanobis model assumed a closed economy; it drew on Soviet planning.

q.s: Borrowing by the States is dealt with in which Article of the Constitution?
q.x: Article 293 covers State borrowing; under 293(3) a State indebted to the Centre needs its consent. Article 292 covers Union borrowing.

q.s: Which of the following statements about borrowing by the States is correct?
o: The Centre cannot attach conditions to such consent.
A State indebted to the Centre needs its consent to raise fresh loans.
Article 292 deals with borrowing by the States.
States can borrow from abroad without restriction.
q.x: Under Article 293(3) consent is needed and conditions may be attached under 293(4); Article 292 covers Union borrowing.

q.s: The First Finance Commission (1951) was chaired by:
q.x: K.C. Neogy chaired the First Finance Commission.

q.s: Which of the following pairs of Finance Commission and Chairman is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: The Fifth FC was chaired by Mahaveer Tyagi; Rajamannar chaired the Fourth.

q.s: Which of the following is excluded from the divisible pool of Central taxes shared with the States?
q.x: Cesses, surcharges and cost of collection are outside the divisible pool, so the 41% share overstates the States' real share.

q.s: The Fifteenth Finance Commission fixed the States' share in the divisible pool of Central taxes at:
q.x: The 15th FC set it at 41% (down from the 14th FC's 42%, after J&K became a UT).

q.s: India's intergovernmental transfers to local bodies are about what share of GDP?
q.x: They are about 0.5% of GDP against 2-5% globally.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the finances of local bodies in India is correct?
o: Transfers to local bodies are about 5% of GDP.
Transfers form a negligible part of ULB revenue.
Weak accounting and balance sheets keep most local bodies out of the bond market.
q.x: Without accrual accounting local bodies cannot tap bonds; transfers are about 0.5% of GDP and about 40% of ULB revenue.

q.s: The Board for Financial Supervision of the RBI (1994) is chaired by the:
q.x: The BFS is chaired by the RBI Governor.

q.s: The Tarapore Committee (1997; 2006) dealt with:
q.x: Both Tarapore Committees examined capital account convertibility; the Bimal Jalan panel scrutinised new bank licences.

q.s: The Reserve Bank of India was nationalised in:
q.x: The RBI Act was passed in 1934, the bank started in 1935 and was nationalised in 1949.

q.s: The setting up of the Reserve Bank of India was recommended by the:
q.x: The Hilton Young Commission (1926) recommended a central bank.

q.s: The Aarogyasri health insurance scheme was launched in undivided Andhra Pradesh in 2007 by the government of:
q.x: Aarogyasri began on 1 April 2007 under YSR.

q.s: The Aarogyasri scheme was originally named after:
q.x: It was launched as Rajiv Aarogyasri.

q.s: The International Financial Services Centres Authority (IFSCA), the unified regulator of IFSCs such as GIFT City, was set up under an Act of:
q.x: The IFSCA Act, 2019 created it (April 2020); PFRDA's Act is of 2013 and IRDAI's of 1999.

q.s: Which of the following pairs of regulator and domain is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: PFRDA (Act of 2013) regulates pensions and the NPS.

q.s: The National Asset Reconstruction Company Ltd (NARCL), the 'bad bank', was announced in the Union Budget of:
q.x: Budget 2021-22 announced NARCL to aggregate stressed loans above ₹500 crore.

q.s: When NARCL acquires a stressed loan, what share of the price does it pay in cash?
q.x: It pays 15% in cash and 85% in government-guaranteed security receipts.

q.s: The Financial Stability and Development Council (FSDC) was set up in:
q.x: The FSDC was set up in December 2010 to coordinate among financial regulators.

q.s: The Financial Stability and Development Council is chaired by the:
q.x: The Finance Minister chairs the FSDC; it also covers financial literacy and inclusion.

q.s: The Plan / Non-plan classification of expenditure in the Union Budget was ended from the Budget of:
q.x: It ended with the 2017-18 Budget; AP too dropped it in its 2017-18 Budget.

q.s: The Plan / Non-plan classification of expenditure was replaced by the:
q.x: From 2017-18 expenditure is shown as revenue and capital.

q.s: Which of the following is a non-debt capital receipt of the Government?
q.x: Recovery of loans and disinvestment are non-debt capital receipts; dividends and interest are non-tax revenue.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a capital receipt of the Government?
q.x: PSU dividends are non-tax revenue receipts.

q.s: The Budget is called the 'Annual Financial Statement' in which Article of the Constitution?
q.x: Article 112 provides for the Annual Financial Statement; Article 110 defines Money Bills.

q.s: The term 'fiscal federalism' was coined by:
q.x: Musgrave coined the term in 1959. 'Fiscal' comes from the Latin fiscus, the public purse.

q.s: In Indian usage, 'deficit financing' means meeting the budget gap by:
o: Borrowing from the RBI, which creates new money
q.x: In India deficit financing means RBI borrowing that adds to the money supply; in Western usage it means any financing of a deficit.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a likely effect of deficit financing by borrowing from the RBI?
o: A fall in the money supply
q.x: RBI-financed deficits create new money and increase the money supply.

q.s: The equalisation levy introduced in India in 2016 applied mainly to:
o: Online advertisement services provided by non-residents
q.x: The 6% levy of 2016 targeted payments to non-resident digital firms for online advertising.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the 2016 equalisation levy is correct?
o: It was a levy under the GST law.
It was levied outside the Income Tax Act, so no credit could be claimed under DTAAs.
It was a part of the Income Tax Act, 1961.
Its credit could be claimed under Double Taxation Avoidance Agreements.
q.x: Being a separate levy outside the Income Tax Act, it was not an income tax covered by DTAAs.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a revenue receipt of the Union Government?
q.x: Recovery of loans is a capital receipt; interest and dividends are non-tax revenue.

q.s: From which year has the Union Budget been presented on 1 February instead of the last working day of February?
q.x: The date was advanced from 2017-18 so that the Budget is passed before 31 March, avoiding a vote on account.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the advancing of the Union Budget to 1 February is correct?
o: It makes a vote on account necessary every year.
It was done to merge the Railway and General Budgets only.
It allows the Budget to be passed before 31 March.
q.x: Presenting it on 1 February lets ministries spend from 1 April without a vote on account.

q.s: The Union Budget 2026-27 was billed as a:
q.x: It was called a 'Yuva Shakti-driven Budget'.

q.s: The three 'Kartavyas' of the Union Budget 2026-27 are growth, human capital and:
q.x: The three Kartavyas are growth, human capital and inclusion.

q.s: The SAARC Currency Swap Framework was instituted by the RBI in:
q.x: It began in 2012; a swap has a tenor of 3 months, rollable twice.

q.s: The first INR drawdown under the 2024-27 SAARC currency swap framework (April 2026) was made by:
q.x: The Maldives made the first INR drawdown under the ₹250 billion INR window.

q.s: The Foreign Investment Promotion Board (FIPB) was abolished in:
q.x: After FIPB was abolished in June 2017, Government-route proposals go through the Foreign Investment Facilitation Portal.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the automatic route for FDI is correct?
o: It needs the prior approval of the administrative ministry.
No prior approval is needed, only post-facto reporting to the RBI.
It needs Cabinet approval above ₹500 crore.
All sectors of the economy are under it.
q.x: Under the automatic route only post-facto reporting is needed; some sectors still need Government approval and some are prohibited.

q.s: The Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership (RCEP) was signed in November 2020 by how many countries?
q.x: Fifteen countries signed it on 15 November 2020; it came into force on 1 January 2022.

q.s: India walked out of the RCEP negotiations in:
q.x: India withdrew in 2019, citing among other things its large trade deficit with China.

q.s: According to the Economic Survey 2025-26, urban wages are about how many times rural wages?
q.x: The Survey puts urban wages at 1.7-2 times rural wages.

q.s: In Andhra Pradesh, tenant cultivators often miss crop insurance and relief in a deficit season mainly because they are missing from the:
q.x: Tenants, who often lack a passbook or KCC, are left out of the e-Crop data used for insurance and relief.

q.s: The largest share of institutional credit to agriculture in India is provided by:
q.x: Commercial banks give about three-fourths; cooperatives give more than RRBs.

q.s: The share of non-institutional sources in rural credit, about 90% in 1950, fell by 2021-22 to about:
q.x: It fell to about 23.4% in 2021-22.

q.s: Rythu Bazars, where farmers sell directly to consumers without commission agents, began in Andhra Pradesh in:
q.x: Rythu Bazars began in 1999 and are run by an Estate Officer; about 129 functioned in 2025-26.

q.s: Under the WTO Agreement on Agriculture, the de minimis limit on amber-box support for developing countries is:
q.x: Developing countries may give amber-box support up to 10% (developed countries 5%).

q.s: Which of the following falls in the 'green box' under the WTO Agreement on Agriculture?
q.x: Research and infrastructure are green box; input subsidies and price support are amber, production-limiting payments blue.

q.s: The goal of a 'socialistic pattern of society', reflected in the Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956, was adopted at the Congress session of:
q.x: The Avadi session of 1955 adopted the goal; the 1956 Resolution was placed before Parliament by Nehru.

q.s: The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956 has been called the:
q.x: With its stress on the public sector it is called the Bible of State Capitalism; it formed the basis of the Second Plan.

q.s: The first Industrial Policy Resolution of independent India was announced in:
q.x: The 1948 Resolution, which listed raw materials, finance, marketing and technology as handicaps of small industries, was followed by the 1956 Resolution.

q.s: Removing licences, quotas and controls without any sale of government equity is called:
q.x: Deregulation frees the market without changing ownership; privatisation transfers ownership or management.

q.s: Sale of a majority stake in a public enterprise together with transfer of management control is called:
q.x: In minority disinvestment the government keeps over 51% and control; a strategic sale hands over control.

q.s: Andhra Pradesh's interest payments in 2026-27 (BE) are about what share of its revenue receipts?
q.x: Interest payments of about ₹37,281 crore are about 16% of receipts, more than double the 2017-18 level.

q.s: Which of the following irrigation projects of Andhra Pradesh has national-project status?
q.x: Polavaram was declared a national project under Section 90 of the AP Reorganisation Act; the others are State projects.

q.s: The Veligonda project in Prakasam region draws water from the:
q.x: Veligonda carries Krishna flood water from the Srisailam reservoir through tunnels; its Phase-I was inaugurated in 2026.

q.s: Which of the following irrigation works of Andhra was taken up earliest?
q.x: Prakasam Barrage (First-Second Plan), Srisailam (Third Plan), Telugu Ganga (Sixth Plan), Jalayagnam (Tenth Plan).

q.s: Jalayagnam, the large irrigation programme of undivided Andhra Pradesh, was launched in:
q.x: Jalayagnam began in 2004 (Tenth Plan); Telugu Ganga was taken up in 1983.

q.s: Under the AP Micro Irrigation Project, SC and ST farmers get a subsidy of:
q.x: SC/ST farmers get full subsidy; other small and marginal farmers get 55% and the rest 45%.

q.s: The Andhra Pradesh Micro Irrigation Project (APMIP) was launched in:
q.x: APMIP began in 2003, long before PMKSY (2015); it now runs as RKVY-Per Drop More Crop.

q.s: In Andhra Pradesh (2023-24), the largest source of gross irrigated area is:
q.x: Wells and tube wells (about 48%) lead canals (about 40%); tanks are a smaller source.

q.s: Which of the following statements about irrigation in Andhra Pradesh (2023-24) is NOT correct?
o: Canals account for about 40% of the gross irrigated area.
Wells and tube wells together account for about 48%.
Eluru district had the largest irrigated area.
Tanks are the largest source of gross irrigated area.
q.x: Wells and tube wells lead; tanks are a minor source. AP has about 19 lakh bore wells.

q.s: Under Andhra Pradesh's MSME Policy (4.0), a special-category micro enterprise gets a capital subsidy of:
q.x: Micro and small special-category units get 45%; a special-category medium unit gets 35% (cap Rs 7 crore).

q.s: PM Vishwakarma, a scheme for traditional artisans, was launched on:
q.x: It was launched on 17 September 2023 (Vishwakarma Jayanti) for FY 2023-24 to 2027-28.

q.s: Under PM Vishwakarma, artisans get collateral-free credit of up to ₹3 lakh at an interest rate of:
q.x: Credit of ₹1 lakh and then ₹2 lakh is given at a concessional 5% for 18 traditional trades.

q.s: The AP Land Titling Act, 2022 sought to move the State from presumptive titling to:
q.x: The Act aimed at State-guaranteed conclusive titles; it was criticised for limiting disputes to the High Court.

q.s: The AP Land Titling Act, 2022 was repealed in:
q.x: It was repealed in 2024; adopting the NITI Aayog Model Act is each State's choice.

q.s: Which State topped the NCAER Land Records and Services Index (N-LRSI) in 2021?
q.x: Madhya Pradesh topped; Andhra Pradesh rose from 10th (2020) to 6th (2021).

q.s: Karnataka's Bhoomi project (2000) was the first to computerise:
o: Records of Rights, Tenancy and Crops
q.x: Bhoomi pioneered computerised RTC land records.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a feature of conclusive land titling?
o: Clear titles allow land to be used as collateral
A single title register replaces separate records
Registration only records a transaction and the title can be challenged
q.x: Registration recording only a transaction is the present presumptive system; under conclusive titling the State guarantees title.

q.s: Sustainable Development Goal 6 relates to:
q.x: SDG 6 is clean water and sanitation; SDG 5 gender equality, SDG 13 climate action, SDG 14 life below water.

q.s: Which of the following pairs of SDG and theme is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: SDG 13 is climate action; life below water is SDG 14.

q.s: Agricultural credit in India is mainly regulated and refinanced by:
