q.x: NABARD is the apex body for agricultural and rural credit.

q.s: Which of the following pairs of regulator and domain is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: SEBI regulates the capital and securities market; agricultural credit is NABARD's domain.

q.s: The Earth is closest to the Sun (perihelion) in:
q.x: Perihelion falls in early January, during the northern winter; the Earth moves fastest then.

q.s: At aphelion the Earth is about how far from the Sun?
q.x: Aphelion (early July) is about 152 million km; perihelion about 147 million km.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: Oblique rays heat less because the same energy is spread over a larger area.
Vertical rays spread energy over a larger area than oblique rays.
The summer hemisphere is the one tilted away from the Sun.
Noon shadows are longest in summer.
q.x: Oblique rays spread energy over more area; the summer hemisphere is tilted towards the Sun, which stands higher and casts shorter noon shadows.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a metamorphic rock?
q.x: Limestone is sedimentary; marble is metamorphosed limestone, slate comes from shale and quartzite from sandstone.

q.s: On metamorphism, coal ultimately changes into:
q.x: Coal passes through anthracite to graphite under heat and pressure.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the seven major lithospheric plates?
q.x: Nazca, like Cocos, Arabian and Philippine, is a minor plate.

q.s: The Kamchatka peninsula, struck by a major earthquake in August 2025, belongs to:
q.x: Kamchatka is in the Russian Far East.

q.s: Flores, struck by an earthquake in August 2026, is an island of:
q.x: Flores is in Indonesia; Mindanao is in the Philippines and Kyushu in Japan.

q.s: An upfold in which the oldest strata lie at the core is called:
q.x: An anticline is an upfold; a syncline is a downfold.

q.s: A fold in which both limbs are parallel to each other is called:
q.x: Isoclinal folds have parallel limbs; a nappe forms after a recumbent fold is thrust forward.

q.s: Hayli Gubbi, a shield volcano that erupted in November 2025 after about 10,000 years, is in:
q.x: Hayli Gubbi lies in the Afar region of Ethiopia.

q.s: Which of the following volcanoes is NOT correctly matched with its country?
q.x: Krakatoa is in Indonesia.

q.s: Which volcano is known as the 'Lighthouse of the Mediterranean'?
q.x: Stromboli erupts every few minutes, hence the name.

q.s: Mount Etna, an active volcano of Italy, is located in:
q.x: Etna is in Sicily; Vesuvius is near Naples.

q.s: Which continent has the largest number of countries?
q.x: Africa has 54 countries.

q.s: Which of the following countries is NOT a part of Oceania?
q.x: Indonesia is part of Asia.

q.s: Which of the following mountain ranges is NOT in Africa?
q.x: The Altai are in Asia; the other three are African ranges.

q.s: The third most abundant gas in dry air is:
q.x: After nitrogen and oxygen, argon (about 0.93%) is third.

q.s: Carbon dioxide makes up about what share of dry air by volume?
q.x: CO2 is about 0.04%; 0.93% is argon.

q.s: Kanchenjunga, the world's third highest peak, lies on the border of:
q.x: Kanchenjunga (8,586 m) is on the Sikkim–Nepal border; Cho Oyu is on the Nepal–Tibet border.

q.s: Namcha Barwa, at the eastern end of the Himalaya, lies near the bend of the:
q.x: Namcha Barwa (7,755 m) overlooks the great bend of the Tsangpo-Brahmaputra.

q.s: The Deccan Traps were formed by:
q.x: Basaltic lava poured out through fissures at the end of the Cretaceous.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Deccan Traps is NOT correct?
o: Their thickness increases from west to east.
They were formed at the end of the Cretaceous period.
Erosion has reduced their original extent.
They were formed by fissure eruptions of basaltic lava.
q.x: The Traps thin from west to east; erosion has reduced them to about 5 lakh sq km.

q.s: The pebble-strewn belt at the foot of the Shiwaliks, where streams disappear underground, is called the:
q.x: Streams sink in the Bhabar and re-emerge in the marshy Terai to its south.

q.s: Which of the following pairs relating to the belts of the Northern Plains is NOT correctly matched?
o: Terai — Marshy belt where streams re-emerge
Bhabar — Pebble belt where streams sink
q.x: Khadar is the newer floodplain alluvium.

q.s: The northern edge of the Northern Plains of India is marked by the:
q.x: The Himalayan Frontal Fault separates the Shiwaliks from the plains; the plains then fall only about 200 m over 1,600 km to the Bay of Bengal.

q.s: The semi-arid strip of the Thar along the Aravallis is called:
q.x: Marusthali is the true desert in the west; Bagar is the semi-arid tract along the Aravallis.

q.s: How many districts has Andhra Pradesh had since 4 April 2022?
q.x: Residual AP had 13 districts after 2014; they were reorganised into 26 on 4 April 2022.

q.s: At its formation on 1 November 1956, Andhra Pradesh had how many districts?
q.x: It had 20 districts; the count rose to 23 with Prakasam, Rangareddy and Vizianagaram.

q.s: Drought identified mainly by a deficiency of soil moisture affecting crops is called:
q.x: Meteorological drought is a rainfall deficit; hydrological drought is reduced streamflow and groundwater.

q.s: Which of the following pairs of drought type and basis is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Hydrological drought refers to reduced streamflow, reservoirs and groundwater.

q.s: In which case did the Supreme Court (2016) direct the creation of a National Disaster Mitigation Fund in the context of drought?
o: Narmada Bachao Andolan v. Union of India
M.C. Mehta v. Union of India
Vellore Citizens' Welfare Forum v. Union of India
Swaraj Abhiyan v. Union of India
q.x: Swaraj Abhiyan (2016) dealt with drought relief and ordered the mitigation fund.

q.s: Under the Manual for Drought Management (2016), the mandatory indicators for declaring drought are:
q.x: Rainfall deviation and dry spells are mandatory; crop sowing and NDVI are impact indicators.

q.s: The final stage of soil erosion by water is:
q.x: Sheet erosion develops into rills and finally gullies; running water is the most powerful agent.

q.s: The most widespread but least noticed type of soil erosion is:
q.x: Sheet erosion removes a thin uniform layer, so it is hardly noticed.

q.s: Which one of the following pairs of tree and region is NOT correctly matched?
o: Sal — Moist deciduous forests of the Terai
Jackfruit — Alpine meadows of the Himalaya
q.x: Jackfruit is an evergreen tree of the Western Ghats; alpine meadows lie above the tree line.

q.s: The leading thorium State of India, with the largest monazite concentration on its coast, is:
q.x: Kerala's coastal sands hold the richest monazite deposits.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a heavy mineral of India's beach sands?
q.x: Beach sands yield ilmenite, rutile, zircon, garnet, sillimanite and monazite; bauxite is a laterite ore.

q.s: Under the MMDR Act, 1957, minor minerals are regulated by the:
q.x: Section 15 gives the States power over minor minerals; petroleum, gas and atomic minerals are outside the Act.

q.s: The MMDR amendment that made auction the only method of allotment and created the District Mineral Foundation was passed in:
q.x: The 2015 amendment introduced auctions, DMF and NMET.

q.s: Which district is first in manganese production in Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: Vizianagaram (Garividi / Garbham) leads; older books name Srikakulam because Garbham lay in pre-1979 Srikakulam district.

q.s: Which district stands first in limestone in Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: Kurnool leads; high-grade limestone also occurs at Jammalamadugu and Mydukur in Kadapa.

q.s: The Jaggayyapeta limestone mine lies in which district?
q.x: Jaggayyapeta is in the old Krishna, now NTR, district.

q.s: In an anticline oil trap under a cap rock, which lies at the top?
q.x: Fluids separate by density: water at the bottom, oil in the middle and gas at the top.

q.s: The Andhra Pradesh Micro Irrigation Project has been running since:
q.x: APMIP began in 2003, long before PMKSY (2015). AP has about 38,862 minor irrigation tanks.

q.s: The ammonia used for making urea is produced by the:
q.x: Ammonia from the Haber process is combined with carbon dioxide to make urea; the Contact process makes sulphuric acid.

q.s: The sulphur used for phosphatic fertilisers in India comes mainly from:
q.x: Recovered sulphur from oil refineries is the main source.

q.s: When private participation in defence production was opened in May 2001, FDI was permitted up to:
q.x: FDI up to 26% was allowed in 2001.

q.s: The 41 units of the Ordnance Factory Board were reorganised into how many Defence PSUs?
q.x: The OFB was dissolved and its units grouped into 7 new DPSUs.

q.s: The Visakhapatnam Steel Plant (RINL), India's first shore-based integrated steel plant, gets its iron ore mainly from:
q.x: RINL, built with USSR technology, draws ore mainly from Bailadila in Chhattisgarh.

q.s: Hindustan Shipyard at Visakhapatnam was set up in 1941 by the:
q.x: Scindia Steam Navigation founded it in 1941.

q.s: Gannavaram airport serves which city?
q.x: Gannavaram is Vijayawada's existing international airport; a greenfield airport is proposed at Dagadarthi in Nellore.

q.s: India's only 'mixed' (natural and cultural) World Heritage Site is:
q.x: Khangchendzonga, Sikkim, is India's only mixed site; Dholavira is the only Harappan WHS.

q.s: Which fort of the 'Maratha Military Landscapes' World Heritage Site is in Tamil Nadu?
q.x: Of its 12 forts, 11 are in Maharashtra and Gingee is in Tamil Nadu.

q.s: NEP 2020 targets a Gross Enrolment Ratio of 50% in higher education by:
q.x: NEP aims at 100% school GER by 2030 and 50% higher-education GER by 2035.

q.s: NIPUN Bharat aims at foundational literacy and numeracy for every child by the end of:
q.x: NIPUN Bharat's goal is FLN by Grade 3, with the deadline moved to 2026-27.

q.s: In the Human Development Report 2025, India is placed in which category?
q.x: India remained in the Medium category, with life expectancy of 72 years and GII rank 102.

q.s: Which of the following statements about India in the Human Development Report 2025 is correct?
o: India moved into the High human development category.
India was placed in the Low human development category.
India's Gender Inequality Index rank fell below 150.
India's life expectancy at birth was 72 years.
q.x: India remained in the Medium category, with life expectancy of 72 years and GII rank improved to 102.

q.s: According to Census 2011, the State with the lowest population density is:
q.x: Arunachal Pradesh had 17 persons per sq km.

q.s: According to Census 2011, which State/UT had the highest population density?
q.x: Delhi had 11,297 persons per sq km, followed by Chandigarh (9,252).

q.s: Podu cultivation, practised by tribes such as the Konda Reddi and Savara, is a form of:
q.x: Podu is shifting cultivation that causes soil erosion and forest fires.

q.s: In Andhra Pradesh, podu cultivation is practised mainly in:
q.x: Podu is concentrated in the tribal Agency districts of ASR and Parvathipuram Manyam.

q.s: According to Census 2011, the least urbanised district of Andhra Pradesh was:
q.x: Srikakulam was only 16.16% urban.

q.s: According to Census 2011, the most urbanised district of Andhra Pradesh was:
q.x: Visakhapatnam (47.45%) led, with Krishna second.

q.s: In physical anthropology, a nasal index of 85 or more is classed as:
q.x: Platyrrhine (broad nose) is 85+; mesorrhine 70-84.9; leptorrhine below 70.

q.s: Which of the following pairs relating to racial classification is NOT correctly matched?
o: Nasal index of 85 or more — Platyrrhine
q.x: Leiotrichi is straight hair, typical of Mongoloids.

q.s: The Dongaria Kondh, who used a 2013 Supreme Court ruling to stop bauxite mining, live in the:
q.x: The Dongaria Kondh of Niyamgiri, Odisha, worship Niyam Raja.

q.s: A community can be added to the Scheduled Tribe list of a State only by:
o: A notification of the State Government
An order of the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes
q.x: Under Article 342(2) only Parliament can modify the ST list, as when the Tamaria were added for Jharkhand in 2022.

q.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Article 343 — Hindi in Devanagari as official language of the Union
Article 345 — Official language(s) of a State
Article 344 — Union's duty to develop Hindi
Article 348 — Language of the Supreme Court and High Courts
q.x: Article 344 provides for the Official Language Commission and Committee; the duty to develop Hindi is in Article 351.

q.s: Which of the following protected areas of Andhra Pradesh was notified earliest?
q.x: Pulicat 1976, NSTR 1983, Koundinya 1990, Papikonda NP 2008.

q.s: Koundinya Wildlife Sanctuary in Chittoor district is known mainly for:
q.x: Koundinya is AP's elephant sanctuary; Pulicat is famous for flamingos.

q.s: COP31 of the UNFCCC in November 2026 is to be held in:
q.x: COP31 meets in Antalya, Türkiye; Brazil hosted COP30, Azerbaijan COP29 and the UAE COP28.

q.s: Uppada, a village facing severe coastal erosion in Andhra Pradesh, lies in the region of:
q.x: Uppada, known also for its sarees, is in the Kakinada region.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the Milankovitch factors of climate change?
q.x: Milankovitch's astronomical theory rests on orbital factors; solar irradiance is not one of them.

q.s: According to the UN World Population Prospects 2022, world population is projected to reach about 9.7 billion by:
q.x: Projections: 8.2 billion in 2025, 8.5 billion in 2030, 9.7 billion in 2050 and 10.4 billion in 2100.

q.s: Which of the following UN World Population Prospects 2022 projections is NOT correct?
q.x: World population is projected at about 10.4 billion in 2100.

q.s: Research and development on fast breeder reactors in India is carried out at:
q.x: The Indira Gandhi Centre for Atomic Research at Kalpakkam leads FBR R&D.

q.s: Which of the following pairs of DAE unit and function is NOT correctly matched?
o: IGCAR, Kalpakkam — Fast breeder reactor R&D
IREL — Beach-sand minerals and rare earths
q.x: AMD explores atomic minerals; heavy water is produced by the Heavy Water Board.

q.s: The Swarnajayanti Fellowship was begun in 1997 to mark:
o: The centenary of the Indian Science Congress
q.x: It was instituted in 1997, the 50th year of Independence.

q.s: Which of the following pairs of fellowship and awarding body is NOT correctly matched?
o: PM Early Career Research Grant — ANRF
Prime Minister's Research Fellowship — Ministry of Education
q.x: The Ramalingaswami Re-entry Fellowship is awarded by the Department of Biotechnology.

q.s: INSPIRE-MANAK awards are meant for students of:
q.x: MANAK targets students of Classes VI-X aged 10-15; SHE is for top UG/PG students.

q.s: The INSPIRE programme is run by the:
q.x: INSPIRE (Innovation in Science Pursuit for Inspired Research) is a DST programme.

q.s: Voice assistants such as Siri and Alexa are examples of:
q.x: They perform specific tasks and are Narrow AI; General AI does not yet exist.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Artificial Intelligence is correct?
o: Superintelligence has been achieved in laboratories.
General AI is already in wide commercial use.
All AI in use today is Narrow AI.
Narrow AI can freely transfer skills across domains.
q.x: All present AI is Narrow; Superintelligence remains hypothetical.

q.s: Ethereum moved from Proof of Work to Proof of Stake through 'The Merge' in:
q.x: The Merge took place in September 2022.

q.s: Under the Proof of Stake mechanism, validators are chosen on the basis of:
o: Random selection by a central bank
q.x: Proof of Stake replaces mining power with staked coins.

q.s: A hydrogen fuel cell produces electricity by:
o: An electrochemical reaction of hydrogen with oxygen
q.x: A fuel cell combines hydrogen and oxygen electrochemically, without combustion, giving electricity, water and heat; efficiency can reach about 55%.

q.s: The by-products of a hydrogen fuel cell are:
q.x: Only water and heat are produced besides electricity.

q.s: The National Solar Mission, launched on 11 January 2010, had a (revised) target of:
q.x: The Solar Mission aimed at 100 GW of solar capacity by 2022.

q.s: The National Mission for Sustaining the Himalayan Ecosystem covers how many thematic areas?
q.x: NMSHE has 12 thematic areas; the Green India Mission was approved on 20 February 2014.

q.s: The rising concentration of persistent toxins such as DDT and mercury along a food chain is called:
q.x: Biomagnification concentrates toxins at higher trophic levels.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a bioremediation technique?
q.x: Bioremediation removes or degrades pollutants; biomagnification concentrates them.

q.s: 3D printing is also known as:
q.x: Objects are built layer by layer from a CAD model, the opposite of subtractive machining.

q.s: In 4D printing, the 'fourth dimension' refers to:
o: Time, as the printed object changes shape over time
q.x: 4D-printed objects use smart materials that change shape over time.

q.s: The term 'Li-Fi' was coined in 2011 by:
q.x: Harald Haas coined Li-Fi, which uses visible light from LEDs.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Li-Fi is correct?
o: It works only with infrared lasers.
Unlike Wi-Fi, it does not pass through walls.
It uses radio waves to transmit data.
It has a longer range than Wi-Fi.
q.x: Li-Fi uses visible LED light, has a shorter range and cannot pass through walls.

q.s: Molten salt energy storage is used mainly in:
q.x: Molten salt stores heat so CSP plants can generate after sunset.

q.s: Which of the following pairs of storage method and principle is NOT correctly matched?
o: Molten salt — Thermal storage in CSP plants
Flywheel — Thermal storage in CSP plants
Pumped storage — Pumping water uphill at low demand
q.x: A flywheel stores rotational kinetic energy.

q.s: PSLV-C37 (15 February 2017) placed how many satellites in orbit in a single launch?
q.x: PSLV-C37 carried a Cartosat-2 series satellite and 103 others, 101 of them foreign nanosatellites.

q.s: The record for the most satellites in one launch, earlier held by PSLV-C37, was broken in 2021 by:
q.x: SpaceX's Transporter-1 carried 143 satellites in 2021.

q.s: The Technology Development Fund of the Ministry of Defence is executed by:
q.x: TDF is a MoD programme executed by DRDO under Make in India.

q.s: Grants under the Technology Development Fund of the MoD are meant mainly for:
q.x: TDF supports MSMEs and start-ups with grants of up to ₹50 crore.

q.s: The first successful test of the BrahMos missile was conducted on 12 June 2001 at:
q.x: BrahMos was first tested at Chandipur, Odisha.

q.s: The BrahMos missile was first inducted into the Indian Navy in 2005 on:
q.x: INS Rajput received it in 2005; it was fired from the moving INS Ranvir in 2010.

q.s: 'Samudra Laksamana' is a naval exercise between India and:
q.x: Samudra Laksamana is the India-Malaysia exercise; its 3rd edition (2024) was off Visakhapatnam.

q.s: How many pillars does the Digital India programme have?
q.x: Digital India has nine pillars, from Broadband Highways to Early Harvest Programmes.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the pillars of Digital India?
q.x: The Smart Cities Mission is a separate urban programme; Electronics Manufacturing aims at net zero imports.

q.s: The isolation of internet users caused by algorithms that rank content by their preferences is called:
q.x: A filter bubble shows users only what matches their preferences.

q.s: Which of the following pairs of term and meaning is NOT correctly matched?
o: Digital footprint — Trail of data left online
Filter bubble — Isolation caused by preference-based algorithms
Cyberbullying — Repeated online harassment of children
Cyber venting — Repeated online harassment of children
q.x: Cyber venting is using websites to pour out one's grievances.

q.s: 'Digital arrest', increasingly reported in India, is:
o: A legal power of the police to detain people online
A cyber security tool of CERT-In
A scam in which fraudsters pose as officials on video calls
A court order blocking a person's internet access
q.x: No law provides for 'digital arrest'; it is a fraud.

q.s: The dark web is usually accessed through:
q.x: The dark web is a hidden part of the internet reached via Tor.

q.s: India's operative national cyber security policy is the National Cyber Security Policy of:
q.x: The 2020 strategy prepared under the National Cyber Security Coordinator is still a draft, so the 2013 policy continues.

q.s: About 80% of India's imported uranium comes from:
q.x: Kazakhstan is India's largest uranium supplier.

q.s: The main hurdle in moving to Stage III of India's three-stage nuclear programme is:
o: Building enough fissile stock in Stage II
q.x: India has huge thorium reserves; the constraint is fissile material from fast breeders. ANEEL fuel combines thorium with HALEU.

q.s: 'Defence in Depth' in nuclear safety means:
o: Storing spent fuel in deep geological sites
Using multiple successive layers of protection
q.x: Defence in Depth relies on successive independent barriers.

q.s: The occupational radiation dose limit, averaged over five years, is:
q.x: It is 20 mSv a year averaged over five years, with no more than 30 mSv in any single year.

q.s: The Partial Test Ban Treaty (PTBT) was signed in:
q.x: PTBT 1963, Seabed Treaty 1971, CTBT 1996; the TPNW entered into force in 2021.

q.s: Which of the following treaties has India signed?
o: Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons
q.x: India signed the PTBT but not the CTBT, TPNW or NPT.

q.s: NITI Aayog's 'Scenarios Towards Viksit Bharat and Net Zero' (2026) recommends nuclear capacity of about 100 GW by 2047 and, by 2070, about:
q.x: The study recommends 200–300 GW of nuclear capacity by 2070.

q.s: India's first wave-energy plant (1991) was set up at:
q.x: The Vizhinjam plant was India's first wave-energy plant.

q.s: India's first Low Temperature Thermal Desalination (LTTD) plant was set up in 2005 at:
q.x: The Kavaratti LTTD plant produces about 1 lakh litres of drinking water a day.

q.s: Bharat Stage VI emission norms were applied nationwide from:
q.x: BS-II came nationwide in 2005, BS-III in 2010, BS-IV in 2017 and BS-VI in 2020.

q.s: Which Bharat Stage emission norm was skipped by India?
q.x: India leapfrogged from BS-IV to BS-VI, skipping BS-V.

q.s: Which State has the largest total coal resources in India?
q.x: Odisha leads in total resources (Jharkhand leads in proved reserves); India's resources were about 400.7 billion tonnes on 1 April 2025.

q.s: Among the world's coal producers, India ranks:
q.x: India has the fifth-largest reserves but is the second-largest producer after China.

q.s: Which village in Gujarat is India's first 24x7 solar-powered village?
q.x: Modhera, known for its Sun Temple, became the first round-the-clock solar village.

q.s: Which was the first Union Territory to run entirely on solar power during daytime?
q.x: Diu was the first UT to meet 100% of its daytime demand from solar; India's first solar ferry 'Aditya' runs in Kerala.

q.s: Which of the following statements about biogeochemical cycles is NOT correct?
o: Photosynthesis removes carbon dioxide from the atmosphere.
Respiration takes up carbon dioxide from the atmosphere.
They involve both biotic and abiotic components.
The phosphorus cycle begins with the weathering of rocks.
q.x: Respiration releases CO2; photosynthesis takes it up.

q.s: Minamata disease in Japan was caused by:
q.x: Methylmercury biomagnified in fish caused Minamata disease; cadmium caused Itai-itai disease.

q.s: The build-up of a pollutant inside a single organism over its lifetime is called:
q.x: Bioaccumulation is within one organism; biomagnification is the rise along a food chain.

q.s: The Living Planet Report, published every two years, is brought out by:
q.x: WWF publishes it biennially; its Living Planet Index tracks vertebrate populations since 1970.

q.s: According to the IPBES Global Assessment (2019), up to how many species face extinction?
q.x: IPBES found about 25% of species threatened, with up to 1 million facing extinction.

q.s: India's first Biodiversity Heritage Site (2007), the Nallur Tamarind Grove, is in:
q.x: Nallur Tamarind Grove is in Karnataka.

q.s: Which of the following Biodiversity Heritage Sites is NOT correctly matched with its State?
q.x: Kasampatty is in Tamil Nadu.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the biodiversity hotspots found in India?
q.x: India's four hotspots are the Himalaya, Indo-Burma, Western Ghats-Sri Lanka and Sundaland (Nicobar).

q.s: Jhum cultivation, logging and hunting are major threats to which hotspot?
q.x: Indo-Burma (north-east India) faces jhum, logging and hunting; Sundaland faced the 2004 tsunami and invasive species.

q.s: According to FAO's Global Forest Resources Assessment 2025, forests cover about what share of the Earth's land?
q.x: Forests cover about 32% of land; annual net loss fell to 4.12 Mha in 2015-2025.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT among the five countries that together hold over half the world's forests?
q.x: The top five are Russia, Brazil, Canada, the USA and China.

q.s: India's first zoo was:
q.x: The Barrackpore menagerie dates from 1800; Alipore opened in 1876.

q.s: The National Wildlife Genetic Resource Bank is located at:
q.x: The genetic resource bank is at Hyderabad's Nehru Zoological Park; the Central Zoo Authority was set up in 1992.

q.s: A State Bill that amends the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 can become law only with the assent of the:
q.x: A State Bill amending a central law on a Concurrent subject needs the President's assent, as with Maharashtra's 2026 leopard Bill.

q.s: The parent Act of the Animal Welfare Board of India is the:
o: Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960
q.x: The AWBI was set up under the PCA Act, 1960.

q.s: Which of the following pairs of Act and purpose is NOT correctly matched?
o: Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960 — Animal Welfare Board of India
Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980 — Diversion of forest land
Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 — Access and benefit sharing
Biological Diversity Act, 2002 — Implementation of the CBD
q.x: Access and benefit sharing is under the Biological Diversity Act; the EP Act is the umbrella environment law.

q.s: The 11th Conference of Parties (COP11) of the Convention on Biological Diversity (2012) was held at:
q.x: Hyderabad hosted CBD COP11; COP14 was at Sharm el-Sheikh and COP16 at Cali.

q.s: Which of the following CBD COPs is NOT correctly matched with its venue?
q.x: COP14 was held at Sharm el-Sheikh, Egypt.

q.s: The Genetic Engineering Appraisal Committee (GEAC) functions under the:
o: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
q.x: GEAC works under MoEFCC under the 1989 Rules framed under the EP Act, 1986.

q.s: The Review Committee on Genetic Manipulation (RCGM) functions under the:
q.x: RCGM, which advises GEAC, is under the DBT.

q.s: GM mustard DMH-11 was developed at Delhi University's CGMCP under the leadership of:
q.x: Deepak Pental led its development.

q.s: GEAC cleared the environmental release of GM mustard DMH-11 in:
q.x: GEAC cleared it in 2022; the Supreme Court gave a split verdict in July 2024.

q.s: Under the Rules, 1989, which body is the first, at the institution level, in the approval chain for genetically engineered organisms?
q.x: The chain is IBSC → RCGM → GEAC → SBCC → DLC.

q.s: Rushikulya, a major mass-nesting (arribada) site of Olive Ridley turtles, is in:
q.x: Rushikulya (Odisha) and beaches of Srikakulam and Vizianagaram see mass nesting.

q.s: The Olive Ridley nesting season on India's east coast is mainly during:
q.x: Nesting runs roughly from November to May; India released its Marine Turtle Action Plan in 2021.

q.s: Under the EPR framework for plastic packaging, 'PIBOs' stands for:
q.x: PIBOs are Producers, Importers and Brand Owners.

q.s: EPR certificates for plastic packaging are generated by recyclers on the portal of the:
q.x: Tradable EPR certificates are generated on the CPCB portal.

q.s: The 'End Plastic Pollution' resolution, which set up the negotiating committee for a global plastics treaty, was adopted at:
q.x: UNEA-5.2 in March 2022 created the Intergovernmental Negotiating Committee (INC).

q.s: Which of the following statements about INC-5.2 of the plastics treaty process (Geneva, August 2025) is correct?
o: It adopted the final treaty text.
It ended without agreeing a treaty text.
It elected Julio Cordano as chair.
q.x: INC-5.2 ended without a text; Julio Cordano was elected chair at INC-5.3 (February 2026).

q.s: Most of the ammonia in India's air comes from:
q.x: About 77-80% of ammonia comes from fertilisers and livestock.

q.s: Ammonium sulphate, nearly one-third of India's PM2.5, forms in the air from ammonia and:
q.x: Ammonia reacts with sulphur dioxide (via sulphuric acid) to form ammonium sulphate.

q.s: Photochemical smog forms when sunlight drives reactions between hydrocarbons and:
q.x: Photochemical (Los Angeles) smog needs hydrocarbons, NOx and sunlight; SO2 marks classical London smog.

q.s: Classical (London) smog forms under:
o: Cold, humid conditions with smoke, fog and sulphur dioxide
Warm, sunny conditions with nitrogen oxides
q.x: London smog is a mix of smoke, fog and SO2 in cold, damp weather.

q.s: The National Clean Air Programme (NCAP) was launched by the MoEFCC in:
q.x: NCAP began in January 2019, targeting a 20-30% cut in PM by 2024 (base 2017) in 130 cities.

q.s: Under NCAP, a 'non-attainment city' is one that has failed to meet:
o: India's National Ambient Air Quality Standards for five years
q.x: Non-attainment cities fail the NAAQS over five years.

q.s: Which of the following is a unit of radioactivity (activity)?
q.x: The becquerel and curie measure activity; gray and rad measure absorbed dose; sievert and rem equivalent dose.

q.s: Which of the following pairs of unit and quantity is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: The curie is a unit of radioactivity, not absorbed dose.

q.s: The Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Cess Act was passed in:
q.x: Water Cess Act 1977, Forest (Conservation) Act 1980, Air Act 1981, PLI Act 1991.

q.s: Which of the following Acts was NOT enacted before 1985?
q.x: The PLI Act came in 1991; the others date from 1977, 1980 and 1981.

q.s: Under the Kigali Amendment, India's baseline years for HFC phase-down are:
q.x: India's baseline is 2024-26; it freezes in 2028 and must cut 85% by 2047.

q.s: Which of the following countries is in the same Kigali Amendment group as India?
q.x: India is in Group 2 with Pakistan, Iran, Iraq and the Gulf States; China is in Group 1.

q.s: The Global Alliance for Climate-Smart Agriculture (GACSA) is a:
o: Voluntary alliance whose membership creates no binding obligations
Fund of the World Bank for farmers
q.x: GACSA is voluntary; members decide their own actions.

q.s: Which of the following fertilisers is NOT suitable for application through fertigation?
q.x: Fertigation uses only soluble fertilisers dissolved in irrigation water; rock phosphate is insoluble.

q.s: Plague spreads to humans from rodents mainly through:
q.x: Plague (Yersinia pestis) is carried by rat fleas.

q.s: Which of the following pairs of zoonotic disease and animal source is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: The reservoir of Nipah is the fruit bat (Pteropus); SARS came via civet cats.

q.s: The HbA1c test indicates:
o: Average blood glucose over the previous 2-3 months
